# Authentication

- oAuth2 authentication.

    - Flow: authorizationCode
    - Authorization URL = [https://www.pinterest.com/oauth/](https://www.pinterest.com/oauth/)
    - Token URL = [https://api.pinterest.com/v5/oauth/token](https://api.pinterest.com/v5/oauth/token)

|Scope|Scope Description|
|---|---|
|ads:read|See all of your advertising data, including ads, ad groups, campaigns etc.|
|ads:write|Create, update, or delete ads, ad groups, campaigns etc.|
|billing:read|See all of your billing data, billing profile, etc.|
|billing:write|Create, update, or delete billing data, billing profiles, etc.|
|biz_access:read|See business access data|
|biz_access:write|Create, update, or delete business access data|
|boards:read|See your public boards, including group boards you join|
|boards:read_secret|See your secret boards|
|boards:write|Create, update, or delete your public boards|
|boards:write_secret|Create, update, or delete your secret boards|
|catalogs:read|See all of your catalogs data|
|catalogs:write|Create, update, or delete your catalogs data|
|msot:write|Create measurement source of truth events|
|pins:read|See your public Pins|
|pins:read_secret|See your secret Pins|
|pins:write|Create, update, or delete your public Pins|
|pins:write_secret|Create, update, or delete your secret Pins|
|user_accounts:read|See your user accounts and followers|
|user_accounts:write|Update your user accounts and followers|

- oAuth2 authentication.

    - Flow: clientCredentials
    - Token URL = [https://api.pinterest.com/v3/oauth/access_token/](https://api.pinterest.com/v3/oauth/access_token/)

|Scope|Scope Description|
|---|---|
|ads:read|See all of your advertising data, including ads, ad groups, campaigns etc.|
|ads:write|Create, update, or delete ads, ad groups, campaigns etc.|
|billing:read|See all of your billing data, billing profile, etc.|
|billing:write|Create, update, or delete billing data, billing profiles, etc.|
|biz_access:read|See business access data|
|biz_access:write|Create, update, or delete business access data|
|boards:read|See your public boards, including group boards you join|
|boards:read_secret|See your secret boards|
|boards:write|Create, update, or delete your public boards|
|boards:write_secret|Create, update, or delete your secret boards|
|catalogs:read|See all of your catalogs data|
|catalogs:write|Create, update, or delete your catalogs data|
|msot:write|Create measurement source of truth events|
|pins:read|See your public Pins|
|pins:read_secret|See your secret Pins|
|pins:write|Create, update, or delete your public Pins|
|pins:write_secret|Create, update, or delete your secret Pins|
|user_accounts:read|See your user accounts and followers|
|user_accounts:write|Update your user accounts and followers|

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer This security scheme applies to the conversion events endpoint (POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/events) and SAN endpoints (POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/san/conversion_events, POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/san/confirmations). These endpoints require a bearer token generated via Ads Manager (ads.pinterest.com).

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: basic

<h1 id="pinterest-rest-api-adaccounts">ad_accounts</h1>

View analytical information about advertising.

Note: If the current operation_user_account (defined by the access token)
has access to another user's Ad Accounts via
<a href='/docs/getting-started/using-business-access/'>Pinterest Business Access</a>,
you can modify your request to use the current operation_user_account's
permissions to those Ad Accounts by including the ad_account_id in the path
parameters for the request (e.g. .../?ad_account_id=12345&...).

## List ad accounts

<a id="opIdad_accounts/list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts`

Get a list of the ad_accounts that the "operation user_account" has access to.
        - This includes ad_accounts they own and ad_accounts that are owned by others who have granted them [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts).

<h3 id="list-ad-accounts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include_shared_accounts|query|boolean|false|Include shared ad accounts|
|bookmark|query|string|false|Cursor used to fetch the next page of items|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Maximum number of items to include in a single page.<br>See documentation on [Pagination](/docs/reference/pagination/) for more information.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "bookmark": "string",
  "items": [
    {
      "country": "AD",
      "created_time": 0,
      "currency": "UNK",
      "id": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "owner": {
        "id": "string",
        "username": "string"
      },
      "permissions": [
        "OWNER"
      ],
      "time_zone": "America/Los_Angeles",
      "updated_time": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

<h3 id="list-ad-accounts-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The request has succeeded.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|The request could not be understood by the server due to unexpected data.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication is required and has either failed or not been provided.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|403|Forbidden|The request was valid, but the server is refusing action. The user might not have the necessary permissions for a resource.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|404|Not Found|The requested resource could not be found on this server.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|

|default|Default|An unexpected error response.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|

|---|---|---|---|---|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
pinterest_oauth2 ( Scopes: ads:read ), client_credentials ( Scopes: ads:read )
</aside>

## Create ad account

<a id="opIdad_accounts/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "country": "AD",
    "currency": "UNK",
    "name": "string",
    "owner_user_id": "string",
    "time_zone": "America/Los_Angeles"
  }'
```

`POST /ad_accounts`

Create a new ad account. Different ad accounts can support different currencies, payment methods, etc.
An ad account is needed to create campaigns, ad groups, and ads; other accounts (your employees or partners) can be assigned business access and appropriate roles to access an ad account.

You can set up up to 50 ad accounts per user. (The user must have a business account to create an ad account.)
For more, see [Create an advertiser account](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/create-an-advertiser-account).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "country": "AD",
  "currency": "UNK",
  "name": "string",
  "owner_user_id": "string",
  "time_zone": "America/Los_Angeles"
}
```

<h3 id="create-ad-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AdAccountCreate](#schemaadaccountcreate)|true|none|
|» country|body|[Country](#schemacountry)|false|Country ID from ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.|
|» currency|body|[Currency](#schemacurrency)|false|Currency Codes from ISO 4217|
|» name|body|string|false|Ad account name.|
|» owner_user_id|body|string|false|Advertiser's owning user ID.|
|» time_zone|body|string|false|The time zone of the ad account, in IANA format (e.g., "America/Los_Angeles"). Adding your local time zone lets you view your campaigns and ad reporting in your preferred time zone. Future reports will be available in both your local time zone and default UTC time zone. Historical data takes 1-2 months to backfill. Your billing and order lines will remain in UTC.|

## Get ad account analytics

<a id="opIdad_account/analytics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/analytics?start_date=1970-01-01&end_date=1970-01-01&columns=SPEND_IN_MICRO_DOLLAR&granularity=TOTAL' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/analytics`

  Get analytics for the specified `ad_account_id`, filtered by the specified options.

  - The token's user_account must either be the Owner of the specified ad account, or have one of the necessary roles granted to them via [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts): Admin, Analyst, Campaign Manager.

  - If granularity is not HOUR, you can pull data from up to 90 days before the current date in UTC time, with a maximum time range of 90 days.

  - If granularity is HOUR, you can pull data from up to 8 days before the current date in UTC time.

<h3 id="get-ad-account-analytics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report start date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days back from today.|
|end_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report end date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days past start_date.|
|columns|query|[[ReportingColumnSync](#schemareportingcolumnsync)]|true|Columns to retrieve, encoded as a comma-separated string. **NOTE**: Any metrics defined as MICRO_DOLLARS returns a value based on the advertiser profile's currency field. For USD, ($1/1,000,000, or $0.000001 - one one-ten-thousandth of a cent). it's microdollars. Otherwise, it's in microunits of the advertiser's currency.<br><br>For example, if the advertiser's currency is GBP (British pound sterling), all MICRO_DOLLARS fields will be in GBP microunits (1/1,000,000 British pound).<br><br>If a column has no value, it may not be returned.|
|granularity|query|[Granularity](#schemagranularity)|true|  TOTAL - metrics are aggregated over the specified date range.<br><br>  DAY - metrics are broken down daily.<br><br>  HOUR - metrics are broken down hourly.<br><br>  WEEK - metrics are broken down weekly.<br><br>  MONTH - metrics are broken down monthly|
|click_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a pin click action. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `30` days.|
|engagement_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for an engagement action. Engagements include saves, closeups, link clicks, and carousel card swipes. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `30` days. **Note:** This parameter no longer returns new data. However, you can still access historic data through **Sept 30, 2027**.|
|view_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a view action. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `1` day.|
|conversion_report_time|query|string|false|The date by which the conversion metrics returned from this endpoint will be reported. There are two dates associated with a conversion event: the date that the user interacted with the ad, and the date that the user completed a conversion event.|
|reporting_timezone|query|[ReportingTimeZone](#schemareportingtimezone)|false|Specify the timezone to be applied for the reporting. This feature is currently in BETA and is not available to all users.|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

## Get advertiser Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) report.

<a id="opIdanalytics/get_mmm_report"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/mmm_reports?token=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```

## Create a request for a Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) report

<a id="opIdanalytics/create_mmm_report"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/mmm_reports \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "advertiser_ids": [
      "string"
    ],
    "columns": [
      "SPEND_IN_DOLLAR"
    ],
    "countries": [
      "US"
    ],
    "custom_column_ids": [
      "string"
    ],
    "end_date": "2020-12-20",
    "granularity": {},
    "level": {},
    "report_name": "string",
    "start_date": "2020-12-20",
    "targeting_types": [
      "GENDER"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/mmm_reports`

    This creates an asynchronous mmm report based on the given request.
    It returns a token that you can use to download the report when it is
    ready. NOTE: An additional limit of 5 queries per minute per advertiser
    applies to this endpoint while it's in beta release.
    For the ADVERTISER_PAID_SPEND_IN_DOLLAR,
    ADVERTISER_PAID_ECPC_IN_DOLLAR, and ADVERTISER_PAID_ECPM_IN_DOLLAR
    columns: if you receive bonus media, this value still includes that spend, and it will
    need to be removed manually with support from your Pinterest account team for a
    fully netted value. Over time, we'll also subtract bonus media and other incentives as
    data becomes available. Production and other non-media fees are excluded.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "advertiser_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "columns": [
    "SPEND_IN_DOLLAR"
  ],
  "countries": [
    "US"
  ],
  "custom_column_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "end_date": "2020-12-20",
  "granularity": {},
  "level": {},
  "report_name": "string",
  "start_date": "2020-12-20",
  "targeting_types": [
    "GENDER"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-request-for-a-marketing-mix-modeling-mmm-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[MMMReportCreate](#schemammmreportcreate)|true|none|
|» advertiser_ids|body|[string]|false|Advertiser IDs for multi-advertiser report|
|» columns|body|[[MMMReportingColumn](#schemammmreportingcolumn)]|true|Metric and entity columns|
|» countries|body|[[TargetingAdvertiserCountry](#schematargetingadvertisercountry)]|false|A List of countries for filtering|
|» custom_column_ids|body|[string]|false|List of custom column IDs|
|» end_date|body|string|true|Metric report end date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD|
|» granularity|body|object|true|  DAY - metrics are broken down daily.<br><br>  WEEK - metrics are broken down weekly.|
|» level|body|object|true|Level of the report|
|» report_name|body|string|true|Name of the Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) report|
|» start_date|body|string|true|Metric report start date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD|
|» targeting_types|body|[[MMMReportingTargetingType](#schemammmreportingtargetingtype)]|true|List of targeting types|

## Get the account analytics report created by the async call

<a id="opIdanalytics/get_report"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/reports?token=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/reports`

  This returns a URL to an analytics report given a token returned from the post request report creation call.
  You can use the URL to download the report. The link is valid for five minutes and the report is valid for one hour.
  - The token's user_account must either be the Owner of the specified ad account, or have one of the necessary roles granted to them via [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts): Admin, Analyst, Campaign Manager.

<h3 id="get-the-account-analytics-report-created-by-the-async-call-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

<a id="opIdanalytics/create_report"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/reports \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/reports`

  This returns a token that you can use to download the report when it is ready.
  Note that this endpoint requires the parameters to be passed as JSON-formatted in the request body. This endpoint does not support URL query parameters.
  - The token's user_account must either be the Owner of the specified ad account, or have one of the necessary roles granted to them via [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts): Admin, Analyst, Campaign Manager.
  - If granularity is not HOUR, you can pull data from up to 914 days before the current date in UTC time, with a maximum time range of 186 days.
  - If granularity is HOUR, you can pull data from up to 8 days before the current date in UTC time, with a maximum time range of 3 days.
  - If level is PRODUCT_ITEM, you can pull data from up to 92 days before the current date in UTC time, with a maximum time range of 31 days.
  - If level is PRODUCT_ITEM, ad_ids and ad_statuses parameters are not allowed. Any columns related to pin promotion and ad is not allowed either.

<h3 id="create-async-request-for-an-account-analytics-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|body|body|[AdsAnalyticsCreateAsyncRequest](#schemaadsanalyticscreateasyncrequest)|true|none|
|» ad_group_ids|body|[[Pinterest.Lib.IntegerFormatType](#schemapinterest.lib.integerformattype)]|false|List of ad group ids|
|» ad_group_statuses|body|[[AdGroupSummaryStatus](#schemaadgroupsummarystatus)]|false|List of values for filtering|
|» ad_ids|body|[[Pinterest.Lib.IntegerFormatType](#schemapinterest.lib.integerformattype)]|false|List of ad ids. This parameter is not supported for Product Item level reports.|
|» ad_statuses|body|[[PinPromotionSummaryStatus](#schemapinpromotionsummarystatus)]|false|List of values for filtering. This parameter is not supported for Product Item level reports.|
|» attribution_types|body|[[ConversionReportAttributionType](#schemaconversionreportattributiontype)]|false|List of attribution types for the conversion report.|
|» campaign_brand_label|body|string|false|Campaign brand label for filtering.|
|» campaign_custom_label|body|string|false|Campaign custom label for filtering.|
|» campaign_ids|body|[[Pinterest.Lib.IntegerFormatType](#schemapinterest.lib.integerformattype)]|false|List of campaign ids|
|» campaign_objective_types|body|array|false|List of values for filtering. ["WEB_SESSIONS"] is in BETA.|
|» campaign_statuses|body|[[CampaignSummaryStatus](#schemacampaignsummarystatus)]|false|List of status values for filtering|
|» click_window_days|body|object|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a pin click action.|
|» columns|body|[[ReportingColumnAsync](#schemareportingcolumnasync)]|false|Metric and entity columns. Pin promotion and ad related columns are not supported for Product Item level reports.|
|» combine_targeting_types|body|boolean|false|Determines if the targeting types included in the request should be consolidated into a single breakdown.|
|» conversion_report_time|body|object|false|Date dimension for conversion metrics.|
|» custom_conversion_event_metrics|body|[[CustomConversionEventMetrics](#schemacustomconversioneventmetrics)]|false|List of advertiser-defined custom conversion event metrics to include in the report|
|» end_date|body|string|true|Metric report end date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD|
|» end_hour|body|integer|false|Which hour of the end date to stop the report (inclusive). Only allowed for hourly reports.|
|» engagement_window_days|body|object|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for an engagement action.|
|» granularity|body|object|true|  TOTAL - metrics are aggregated over the specified date range.<br>  DAY - metrics are broken down daily.<br>  HOUR - metrics are broken down hourly.<br>  WEEKLY - metrics are broken down weekly.<br>  MONTHLY - metrics are broken down monthly.|
|» level|body|object|false|Level of the report|
|» metrics_filters|body|[[AdsAnalyticsMetricsFilter](#schemaadsanalyticsmetricsfilter)]|false|List of metrics filters|
|» primary_sort|body|object|false|none|
|» product_group_ids|body|[[Pinterest.Lib.IntegerFormatType](#schemapinterest.lib.integerformattype)]|false|List of product group ids|
|» product_group_statuses|body|[[ProductGroupSummaryStatus](#schemaproductgroupsummarystatus)]|false|List of values for filtering|
|» product_item_ids|body|[[Pinterest.Lib.IntegerFormatType](#schemapinterest.lib.integerformattype)]|false|List of product item ids|
|» report_format|body|object|false|none|
|» reporting_timezone|body|object|false|Specify the timezone to be applied for the reporting.|
|» start_date|body|string|true|Metric report start date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD|
|» start_hour|body|integer|false|Which hour of the start date to begin the report. Only allowed for hourly reports.|
|» targeting_types|body|[[AdAdsAnalyticsAsyncTargetingTypes](#schemaadadsanalyticsasynctargetingtypes)]|false|List of targeting types. Requires `level` to be a value ending in `_TARGETING`.|
|» view_window_days|body|object|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a view action.|

## Get advertiser brand, category, SKU report

<a id="opIdanalytics/get_conversion_product_report"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/reports/brand_category_sku?token=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/reports/brand_category_sku`

  [Restricted](/docs/getting-started/using-beta-and-restricted-features/)
  Get a brand, category, SKU report for an ad account. This call returns the URL for the report that matches the token returned in the request to the Create brand, category, SKU report endpoint.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|token|query|string|true|Token returned from the post request creation call|

## Create a request for a brand, category, SKU report

<a id="opIdanalytics/create_conversion_product_report"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/reports/brand_category_sku \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ad_group_ids": [
      "12345678"
    ],
    "campaign_ids": [
      "12345678"
    ],
    "campaign_objective_types": [
      "AWARENESS"
    ],
    "click_window_days": 30,
    "columns": [
      "AD_GROUP_ID"
    ],
    "conversion_product_attribution_type": "DEFAULT",
    "conversion_product_breakdown": "PRODUCT_BRAND",
    "conversion_report_time": "TIME_OF_AD_ACTION",
    "end_date": "2024-04-23",
    "granularity": {},
    "level": {},
    "product_sku_ids": [
      "WBC45678",
      "WBC45679"
    ],
    "report_name": "string",
    "start_date": "2024-04-17",
    "view_window_days": 30
  }'
```

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/reports/brand_category_sku`

  [Restricted](/docs/getting-started/using-beta-and-restricted-features/)
  This creates an asynchronous brand, category, SKU report based on the given request. This request returns a token that you can use to download the report when it is ready.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ad_group_ids": [
    "12345678"
  ],
  "campaign_ids": [
    "12345678"
  ],
  "campaign_objective_types": [
    "AWARENESS"
  ],
  "click_window_days": 30,
  "columns": [
    "AD_GROUP_ID"
  ],
  "conversion_product_attribution_type": "DEFAULT",
  "conversion_product_breakdown": "PRODUCT_BRAND",
  "conversion_report_time": "TIME_OF_AD_ACTION",
  "end_date": "2024-04-23",
  "granularity": {},
  "level": {},
  "product_sku_ids": [
    "WBC45678",
    "WBC45679"
  ],
  "report_name": "string",
  "start_date": "2024-04-17",
  "view_window_days": 30
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-request-for-a-brand-category-sku-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|body|body|[ConversionProductReportCreate](#schemaconversionproductreportcreate)|true|none|
|» ad_group_ids|body|[[Pinterest.Lib.IntegerFormatType](#schemapinterest.lib.integerformattype)]|false|  List of ad group ids.<br>  Only support ad_group_ids field when level of the report is AD_GROUP.|
|» campaign_ids|body|[[Pinterest.Lib.IntegerFormatType](#schemapinterest.lib.integerformattype)]|false|  List of campaign ids.<br>  Only support campaign_ids field when level of the report is CAMPAIGN.|
|» campaign_objective_types|body|[[ConversionObjectiveType](#schemaconversionobjectivetype)]|false|List of values for filtering. Default is ['CONSIDERATION','AWARENESS','WEB_CONVERSION','VIDEO_COMPLETION'].|
|» click_window_days|body|object|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a pin click action. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `30` days.|
|» columns|body|[[ConversionProductReportingColumn](#schemaconversionproductreportingcolumn)]|true|Metric and entity columns|
|» conversion_product_attribution_type|body|object|false|  Required attribution type of the B/C/S report.<br>  When the attribution type is BRAND_ATTRIBUTION, start_date for the report must be after 2025-04-01.|
|» conversion_product_breakdown|body|object|false|Report breakdown type. This is used to specify the breakdown of the report by brand, category, or SKU.|
|» conversion_report_time|body|object|false|The date by which the conversion metrics returned from this endpoint will be reported. There are two dates associated with a conversion event: the date that the user interacted with the ad, and the date that the user completed a conversion event.|
|» end_date|body|string|true|  Metric report end date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD.<br>  A max of 1 year is allowed between the start and end date for reports.|
|» granularity|body|object|true|Report granularity for time-based metric aggregation|
|» level|body|object|true|Level of the report|
|» product_sku_ids|body|[[Pinterest.Lib.AlphaNumericFormatType](#schemapinterest.lib.alphanumericformattype)]|false|  List of SKU ids.<br>  Only support product_sku_ids field when report breakdown type is PRODUCT_SKU_GROUP.|
|» report_name|body|string|true|Name of the conversion product report|
|» start_date|body|string|true|  Metric report start date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD.<br>  Start date must be after 2024-03-16. 7 day minimum time window for report is required.|
|» view_window_days|body|object|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a view action. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `1` day.|

## Delete ads data for ad account in API Sandbox

<a id="opIdsandbox/delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/sandbox \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/sandbox`

Delete an ad account and all the ads data associated with that account.
A string message is returned indicating the status of the delete operation.

Note: This endpoint is only allowed in the Pinterest API Sandbox (https://api-sandbox.pinterest.com/v5).
Go to /docs/developer-tools/sandbox/ for more information.

<h3 id="delete-ads-data-for-ad-account-in-api-sandbox-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

## Get targeting analytics for an ad account

<a id="opIdad_account_targeting_analytics/get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/targeting_analytics?start_date=1970-01-01&end_date=1970-01-01&targeting_types=APPTYPE&columns=SPEND_IN_MICRO_DOLLAR&granularity=TOTAL' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/targeting_analytics`

Get targeting analytics for an ad account.
For the requested account and metrics, the response will include the requested metric information
(e.g. SPEND_IN_DOLLAR) for the requested target type (e.g. "age_bucket") for applicable values (e.g. "45-49"). <p/>

* The token's user_account must either be the Owner of the specified ad account, or have one of the necessary roles granted to them via [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts): Admin, Analyst, Campaign Manager.
* If granularity is not HOUR, you can pull data from up to 90 days before the current date in UTC time, with a maximum time range of 90 days.
* If granularity is HOUR, you can pull data from up to 8 days before the current date in UTC time, with a maximum time range of 3 days.

<h3 id="get-targeting-analytics-for-an-ad-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|start_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report start date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days back from today.|
|end_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report end date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days past start_date.|
|targeting_types|query|[[AdsAnalyticsAccountTargetingType](#schemaadsanalyticsaccounttargetingtype)]|true|Targeting type breakdowns for the report. The reporting per targeting type is independent from each other. ["AGE_BUCKET_AND_GENDER"] is in BETA and not yet available to all users.|
|columns|query|[[ReportingColumnSync](#schemareportingcolumnsync)]|true|Columns to retrieve, encoded as a comma-separated string. **NOTE**: Any metrics defined as MICRO_DOLLARS returns a value based on the advertiser profile's currency field. For USD, ($1/1,000,000, or $0.000001 - one one-ten-thousandth of a cent). it's microdollars. Otherwise, it's in microunits of the advertiser's currency.<br><br>For example, if the advertiser's currency is GBP (British pound sterling), all MICRO_DOLLARS fields will be in GBP microunits (1/1,000,000 British pound).<br><br>If a column has no value, it may not be returned.|
|granularity|query|[Granularity](#schemagranularity)|true|  TOTAL - metrics are aggregated over the specified date range.<br><br>  DAY - metrics are broken down daily.<br><br>  HOUR - metrics are broken down hourly.<br><br>  WEEK - metrics are broken down weekly.<br><br>  MONTH - metrics are broken down monthly|
|click_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a pin click action. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `30` days.|
|engagement_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for an engagement action. Engagements include saves, closeups, link clicks, and carousel card swipes. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `30` days. **Note:** This parameter no longer returns new data. However, you can still access historic data through **Sept 30, 2027**.|
|view_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a view action. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `1` day.|
|conversion_report_time|query|string|false|The date by which the conversion metrics returned from this endpoint will be reported. There are two dates associated with a conversion event: the date that the user interacted with the ad, and the date that the user completed a conversion event.|
|attribution_types|query|[[ConversionReportAttributionType](#schemaconversionreportattributiontype)]|false|List of types of attribution for the conversion report|
|reporting_timezone|query|[ReportingTimeZone](#schemareportingtimezone)|false|Specify the timezone to be applied for the reporting. This feature is currently in BETA and is not available to all users.|

## Create async request for an analytics report using a template

<a id="opIdanalytics/create_template_report"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/templates/string/reports \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/templates/{template_id}/reports`

  This takes a template ID and an optional custom timeframe and
  constructs an asynchronous report based on the template. It returns
  a token that you can use to download the report when it is ready.

<h3 id="create-async-request-for-an-analytics-report-using-a-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|none|
|template_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of a template.|
|start_date|query|string(date)|false|Metric report start date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 2.5 years back from today.|
|end_date|query|string(date)|false|Metric report end date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 2.5 years past start date.|
|granularity|query|[Granularity](#schemagranularity)|false|  TOTAL - metrics are aggregated over the specified date range.<br><br>  DAY - metrics are broken down daily.<br><br>  HOUR - metrics are broken down hourly.<br><br>  WEEK - metrics are broken down weekly.<br><br>  MONTH - metrics are broken down monthly|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|granularity|TOTAL|
|granularity|DAY|
|granularity|HOUR|
|granularity|WEEK|
|granularity|MONTH|

## List ad groups

<a id="opIdad_groups/list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/ad_groups \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/ad_groups`

List ad groups based on provided campaign IDs or ad group IDs.(campaign_ids or ad_group_ids).
**Note:** Provide only campaign_id or ad_group_id. Do not provide both.

<h3 id="list-ad-groups-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bookmark|query|string|false|Cursor used to fetch the next page of items|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Maximum number of items to include in a single page.<br>See documentation on [Pagination](/docs/reference/pagination/) for more information.|
|order|query|[Pinterest.Lib.PaginationOrder](#schemapinterest.lib.paginationorder)|false|The order in which to sort the items returned: "ASCENDING" or "DESCENDING" by ID.<br>Note that higher-value IDs are associated with more-recently added items.|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|campaign_ids|query|[[CampaignIdType](#schemacampaignidtype)]|false|List of Campaign Ids to use to filter the results.|
|ad_group_ids|query|[[Pinterest.Lib.IntegerFormatType](#schemapinterest.lib.integerformattype)]|false|List of Ad group Ids to retrieve keywords from. This feature is currently in BETA and is not available to all users.|
|entity_statuses|query|[[EntityStatus](#schemaentitystatus)]|false|Entity status|
|translate_interests_to_names|query|boolean|false|Return interests as text names (if value is true) rather than topic IDs.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|ASCENDING|
|order|DESCENDING|
|entity_statuses|ACTIVE|
|entity_statuses|PAUSED|
|entity_statuses|ARCHIVED|
|entity_statuses|DRAFT|
|entity_statuses|DELETED_DRAFT|

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/ad_groups`

Create multiple new ad groups. All ads in a given ad group will have the same budget, bid, run dates, targeting, and placement (search, browse, other).

For more information, [click here](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/campaign-structure).

**Notes:**
- `bid_in_micro_currency` and `budget_in_micro_currency` should be expressed in microcurrency amounts based on the currency field set in the advertiser's profile.

Microcurrency is used to track very small transactions, based on the currency set in the advertiser's profile. A microcurrency unit is 10^(-6) of the standard unit of currency selected in the advertiser's profile.

**Equivalency equations**, using dollars as an example currency:
- $1 = 1,000,000 microdollars
- 1 microdollar = $0.000001

**To convert between currency and microcurrency**, using dollars as an example currency:
- To convert dollars to microdollars, multiply dollars by 1,000,000
- To convert microdollars to dollars, divide microdollars by 1,000,000

- Ad groups belong to ad campaigns. Some types of campaigns (e.g. budget optimization) have limits on the number of ad groups they can hold. If you exceed those limits, you will get an error message.
- Certain organizations with [closed beta](/docs/getting-started/using-beta-and-restricted-features/) access can set `start_time` and `end_time` at the ad group level for campaigns with Campaign Budget Optimization (CBO) objectives: `TRAFFIC`, `AWARENESS`, `WEB_CONVERSIONS`, and `CATALOG_SALES`. All other organizations can set these scheduling parameters for non-CBO campaigns only.
- If the parent ad campaign has start and end times set, ad group start and end times must occur within the parent campaign schedule.

## Get ad group analytics

<a id="opIdad_groups/analytics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/ad_groups/analytics?start_date=1970-01-01&end_date=1970-01-01&ad_group_ids=string&columns=SPEND_IN_MICRO_DOLLAR&granularity=TOTAL' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/ad_groups/analytics`

Get analytics for the specified ad groups in the specified `ad_account_id`, filtered by the specified options.

- The token's user_account must either be the Owner of the specified ad account, or have one of the necessary roles granted to them via [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts): Admin, Analyst, Campaign Manager.
- If granularity is not HOUR, you can pull data from up to 90 days before the current date in UTC time, with a maximum time range of 90 days.
- If granularity is HOUR, you can pull data from up to 8 days before the current date in UTC time, with a maximum time range of 3 days.

<h3 id="get-ad-group-analytics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report start date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days back from today.|
|end_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report end date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days past start_date.|
|ad_group_ids|query|[[AdGroupIdType](#schemaadgroupidtype)]|true|List of Ad group Ids to use to filter the results.|
|columns|query|[[ReportingColumnSync](#schemareportingcolumnsync)]|true|Columns to retrieve, encoded as a comma-separated string. **NOTE**: Any metrics defined as MICRO_DOLLARS returns a value based on the advertiser profile's currency field. For USD, ($1/1,000,000, or $0.000001 - one one-ten-thousandth of a cent). it's microdollars. Otherwise, it's in microunits of the advertiser's currency.<br><br>For example, if the advertiser's currency is GBP (British pound sterling), all MICRO_DOLLARS fields will be in GBP microunits (1/1,000,000 British pound).<br><br>If a column has no value, it may not be returned.|
|granularity|query|[Granularity](#schemagranularity)|true|  TOTAL - metrics are aggregated over the specified date range.<br><br>  DAY - metrics are broken down daily.<br><br>  HOUR - metrics are broken down hourly.<br><br>  WEEK - metrics are broken down weekly.<br><br>  MONTH - metrics are broken down monthly|
|click_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a pin click action. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `30` days.|
|engagement_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for an engagement action. Engagements include saves, closeups, link clicks, and carousel card swipes. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `30` days. **Note:** This parameter no longer returns new data. However, you can still access historic data through **Sept 30, 2027**.|
|view_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a view action. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `1` day.|
|conversion_report_time|query|string|false|The date by which the conversion metrics returned from this endpoint will be reported. There are two dates associated with a conversion event: the date that the user interacted with the ad, and the date that the user completed a conversion event.|
|aggregate_report_rows|query|boolean|false|Determines if report rows should be aggregated across all requested entities. This feature is currently in BETA and is not available to all users.|
|reporting_timezone|query|[ReportingTimeZone](#schemareportingtimezone)|false|Specify the timezone to be applied for the reporting. This feature is currently in BETA and is not available to all users.|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/ad_groups/audience_sizing`

Get potential audience size for an ad group with given targeting criteria.
Potential audience size estimates the number of people you may be able to reach per month with your campaign.
It is based on historical advertising data and the targeting criteria you select.
It does not guarantee results or take into account factors such as bid, budget, schedule, seasonality or product experiments.

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/ad_groups/targeting_analytics?ad_group_ids=string&start_date=1970-01-01&end_date=1970-01-01&targeting_types=APPTYPE&columns=SPEND_IN_MICRO_DOLLAR&granularity=TOTAL' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/ad_groups/targeting_analytics`

Get targeting analytics for one or more ad groups. For the requested ad group(s) and metrics, the response will include the requested metric information (e.g. SPEND_IN_DOLLAR) for the requested target type (e.g. "age_bucket") for applicable values (e.g. "45-49").

- The token's user_account must either be the Owner of the specified ad account, or have one of the necessary roles granted to them via [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts): Admin, Analyst, Campaign Manager.
- If granularity is not HOUR, you can pull data from up to 90 days before the current date in UTC time, with a maximum time range of 90 days.
- If granularity is HOUR, you can pull data from up to 8 days before the current date in UTC time, with a maximum time range of 3 days.

<h3 id="get-targeting-analytics-for-ad-groups-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|ad_group_ids|query|[[AdGroupIdType](#schemaadgroupidtype)]|true|List of Ad group Ids to use to filter the results.|
|start_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report start date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days back from today.|
|end_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report end date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days past start_date.|
|targeting_types|query|[[AdsAnalyticsAdGroupTargetingType](#schemaadsanalyticsadgrouptargetingtype)]|true|Targeting type breakdowns for the report. The reporting per targeting type is independent from each other. ["AGE_BUCKET_AND_GENDER", "CREATIVE_ENHANCEMENTS"] are in BETA and not yet available to all users.|
|columns|query|[[ReportingColumnSync](#schemareportingcolumnsync)]|true|Columns to retrieve, encoded as a comma-separated string. **NOTE**: Any metrics defined as MICRO_DOLLARS returns a value based on the advertiser profile's currency field. For USD, ($1/1,000,000, or $0.000001 - one one-ten-thousandth of a cent). it's microdollars. Otherwise, it's in microunits of the advertiser's currency.<br><br>For example, if the advertiser's currency is GBP (British pound sterling), all MICRO_DOLLARS fields will be in GBP microunits (1/1,000,000 British pound).<br><br>If a column has no value, it may not be returned.|
|granularity|query|[Granularity](#schemagranularity)|true|  TOTAL - metrics are aggregated over the specified date range.<br><br>  DAY - metrics are broken down daily.<br><br>  HOUR - metrics are broken down hourly.<br><br>  WEEK - metrics are broken down weekly.<br><br>  MONTH - metrics are broken down monthly|
|click_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a pin click action. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `30` days.|
|engagement_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for an engagement action. Engagements include saves, closeups, link clicks, and carousel card swipes. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `30` days. **Note:** This parameter no longer returns new data. However, you can still access historic data through **Sept 30, 2027**.|
|view_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a view action. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `1` day.|
|conversion_report_time|query|string|false|The date by which the conversion metrics returned from this endpoint will be reported. There are two dates associated with a conversion event: the date that the user interacted with the ad, and the date that the user completed a conversion event.|
|attribution_types|query|[[ConversionReportAttributionType](#schemaconversionreportattributiontype)]|false|List of types of attribution for the conversion report|
|reporting_timezone|query|[ReportingTimeZone](#schemareportingtimezone)|false|Specify the timezone to be applied for the reporting. This feature is currently in BETA and is not available to all users.|
|sort_columns|query|[string]|false|Sort Columns.|
|sort_ascending|query|boolean|false|Sort ascending.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The request has succeeded.|[MetricsResponse](#schemametricsresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|The request could not be understood by the server due to unexpected data.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication is required and has either failed or not been provided.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|403|Forbidden|The request was valid, but the server is refusing action. The user might not have the necessary permissions for a resource.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|404|Not Found|The requested resource could not be found on this server.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|429|Too Many Requests|The user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time and is being rate limited.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|default|Default|An unexpected error response.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
pinterest_oauth2 ( Scopes: ads:read ), client_credentials ( Scopes: ads:read )
</aside>

## Get ad group

<a id="opIdad_groups/get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/ad_groups/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/ad_groups/{ad_group_id}`

Get a specific ad group given the ad group ID.

<h3 id="get-ad-group-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_group_id|path|string|true|Ad group ID.|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/bid_floor`

List bid floors for your campaign configuration. Bid floors are given in microcurrency values based on the currency in the bid floor specification.

Microcurrency is used to track very small transactions, based on the currency set in the advertiser's profile.

A microcurrency unit is 10^(-6) of the standard unit of currency selected in the advertiser's profile.

**Equivalency equations**, using dollars as an example currency:

* $1 = 1,000,000 microdollars
* 1 microdollar = $0.000001

**To convert between currency and microcurrency**, using dollars as an example currency:

* To convert dollars to microdollars, mutiply dollars by 1,000,000
* To convert microdollars to dollars, divide microdollars by 1,000,000

For more on bid floors see [Set your bid](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/set-your-bid).

> Body parameter

```json
    {
      "billable_event": {},
      "countries": [

      ],
      "creative_type": {},
      "currency": {},

      "optimization_goal_metadata": {

          },

          "reporting_event": "string"
        },

          "frequency": 2,
          "timerange": "THIRTY_DAY"
        },
        "scrollup_goal_metadata": {

        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "targeting_spec": {
    "AGE_BUCKET": [
      "18-24"
    ],
    "APPTYPE": [
      "android_mobile"
    ],
    "AUDIENCE_EXCLUDE": [
      "string"
    ],

    ],

    ],

      "string"

      "string"
```

<h3 id="get-bid-floors-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|body|body|[BidFloorCreate](#schemabidfloorcreate)|true|none|
|» bid_floor_specs|body|[[BidFloorSpec](#schemabidfloorspec)]|true|List of bid floor specifications.|
|» targeting_spec|body|object|false|Ad group targeting specification defining the ad group target audience.|
|» » AGE_BUCKET|body|[[TargetingSpecAgeBucket](#schematargetingspecagebucket)]|false|**Legacy field.** Predefined age ranges. We recommend using MINIMUM_AGE and MAXIMUM_AGE instead for more flexible targeting. Cannot be combined with MINIMUM_AGE/MAXIMUM_AGE. If neither AGE_BUCKET nor MINIMUM_AGE/MAXIMUM_AGE are specified, all ages will be targeted.|
|» » APPTYPE|body|[[TargetingSpecAppType](#schematargetingspecapptype)]|false|Allowed devices. If the APPTYPE field is missing, the default behavior in terms of ad delivery is that **All devices/apptypes** will be targeted.|
|» » AUDIENCE_EXCLUDE|body|[[Pinterest.Lib.IntegerFormatType](#schemapinterest.lib.integerformattype)]|false|Excluded customer list IDs. Used to drive new customer acquisition goals. For example: ["2542620905475"]. Audience lists need to have at least 100 people with Pinterest accounts in them. If the AUDIENCE_EXCLUDE field is missing, the default behavior in terms of ad delivery is that **No users will be excluded**.|
|» » AUDIENCE_INCLUDE|body|[[Pinterest.Lib.IntegerFormatType](#schemapinterest.lib.integerformattype)]|false|Targeted customer list IDs. For example: ["2542620905473"]. Audience lists need to have at least 100 people with Pinterest accounts in them Audience lists need to have at least 100 people with Pinterest accounts in them. If the AUDIENCE_INCLUDE field is missing, the default behavior in terms of ad delivery is that **All users will be included**.|
|» » GENDER|body|[[TargetingSpecGender](#schematargetingspecgender)]|false|Targeted genders. Values: ["unknown","male","female"]. If the GENDER field is missing, the default behavior in terms of ad delivery is that **All genders will be targeted**.|
|» » GEO|body|[string]|false|Region codes or postal codes to include for targeting.<br><br>Region codes represent broader geographical areas. Example: `US-CA` is the region code for California in the United States.<br><br>Postal codes represent more granular, specific areas. Example: `94103` is a postal code for a specifc area in San Francisco, California, U.S.A.<br><br>For each ad group, use only one of these methods, depending on which fits your targeting needs. Do not use both. For example, either specify a broader region code like `US-CA` or a more granular postal code within that regon, such as `94103`.<br><br>You can specify multiple region codes or postal codes in an array, depending on which method you choose.<br><br>Precede a region code array with the `region_codes` key and a postal code value with the `postal_codes` key. Examples:<br><br>```<br>"geo": {<br>  "region_codes": ["US-CA"]<br>}<br>```<br><br>```<br>"geo": {<br>  "postal_codes": ["94103"]<br>}<br>```<br><br>For each ad group, specify at least one `GEO` or `LOCATION`.<br><br>If you do not specifiy a `GEO` code, only `LOCATION` values will be targeted (See `LOCATION` parameter in this targeting spec.).<br><br>Learn how to [get a current, complete list of codes](/docs/analytics-and-reports/ads-reporting/#get-all-available-codes-and-zones).|
|» » GEO_EXCLUDE|body|[string]|false|[Closed beta](/docs/getting-started/using-beta-and-restricted-features/)<br><br>Region codes or postal codes to exclude from the targeting inclusion area.<br><br>See `GEO` parameter in this targeting spec for rules, syntax, and other information.|
|» » INTEREST|body|[string]|false|Array of interest object IDs. If the INTEREST field is missing, the default behavior in terms of ad delivery is that **All interests will be targeted**.|
|» » LOCALE|body|[string]|false|24 ISO 639-1 two-letter language codes. If the LOCALE field is not included in the request, all languages are targeted.|
|» » LOCATION|body|[string]|false|Metropolitan codes and/or ISO-Alpha-2, two-letter country codes to include for targeting.<br><br>Precede country code values with the `country_codes` key and metro code values with `metro_codes` key. Example:<br><br>```<br>"location": {<br>  "country_codes": ["US", "CA"],<br>  "metro_codes": ["501", "602"]<br>}<br>```<br><br>For each ad group, specify at least one `GEO` or `LOCATION` code.<br><br>If you do not specify a `LOCATION` code, only `GEO` values will be targeted (See `GEO` parameter in this targeting spec.).<br><br>Learn how to [get a current, complete list of codes](/docs/analytics-and-reports/ads-reporting/#get-all-available-codes-and-zones).|
|» » LOCATION_EXCLUDE|body|[string]|false|[Closed beta](/docs/getting-started/using-beta-and-restricted-features/)<br><br>Metropolitan codes and/or ISO-Alpha-2, two-letter country codes to exclude from targeting.<br><br>See `LOCATION` parameter in this targeting spec for rules, syntax, and other information.|
|» » MAXIMUM_AGE|body|string|false|Maximum age to target (inclusive). Values: "18", "19", ..., "65", "65+". Must be used together with `MINIMUM_AGE`. Cannot be combined with `AGE_BUCKET`. If neither `MINIMUM_AGE`/`MAXIMUM_AGE` nor `AGE_BUCKET` are specified, all ages will be targeted.|
|» » MINIMUM_AGE|body|string|false|Minimum age to target (inclusive). Values: "18", "19", ..., "65". Note: 65+ is not allowed for minimum age. Must be used together with `MAXIMUM_AGE`. Cannot be combined with `AGE_BUCKET`. If neither `MINIMUM_AGE`/`MAXIMUM_AGE` nor `AGE_BUCKET` are specified, all ages will be targeted.|
|» » SHOPPING_RETARGETING|body|[[TargetingSpecShoppingRetargeting](#schematargetingspecshoppingretargeting)]|false|Array of object: lookback_window [Integer]: Number of days ago to start lookback timeframe for dynamic retargeting tag_types [Array of integer]: Event types to target for dynamic retargeting exclusion_window [Integer]: Number of days ago to stop lookback timeframe for dynamic retargeting|
|» » TARGETING_STRATEGY|body|[[TargetingStrategy](#schematargetingstrategy)]|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|» » AGE_BUCKET|19+|
|» » AGE_BUCKET|20+|
|» » AGE_BUCKET|21+|
|» » AGE_BUCKET|25-34|

## Create ad preview with pin or image

<a id="opIdad_previews/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/ad_previews \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "image_url": "https://somewebsite.com/someimage.jpg",
    "title": "My Preview Image"
  }'
```

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/ad_previews`

Create an ad preview given an ad account ID and either an existing organic pin ID or the URL for an image to be used to create the Pin and the ad.

If you are creating a preview from an existing Pin, that Pin must be promotable: that is, it must have a clickthrough link and meet other requirements. (See [Ads Overview](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/promoted-pins-overview).)

You can view the returned preview URL on a webpage or iframe for 7 days, after which the URL expires. Collection ads are not currently supported ad preview.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "image_url": "https://somewebsite.com/someimage.jpg",
  "title": "My Preview Image"
}
```

<h3 id="create-ad-preview-with-pin-or-image-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|body|body|[AdPreviewRequest](#schemaadpreviewrequest)|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[AdPreviewSourceImage](#schemaadpreviewsourceimage)|false|Ad preview source from an image URL.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[AdPreviewSourcePinId](#schemaadpreviewsourcepinid)|false|Ad preview source from an existing Pin.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[AdPreviewShopping](#schemaadpreviewshopping)|false|Ad preview from a catalog product group (shopping).|

## List ads

<a id="opIdads/list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/ads \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/ads`

List ads that meet the filters provided:
    - Listed campaign ids or ad group ids or ad ids
    - Listed entity statuses

If no filter is provided, all ads in the ad account are returned.

**Note:**
Provide only `campaign_id` or `ad_group_id` or `ad_id`. Do not provide more than one type.

Review status is provided for each ad; if `review_status` is `REJECTED`, the `rejected_reasons` field will contain additional information.

For more, see [Pinterest advertising standards](https://policy.pinterest.com/en/advertising-guidelines).

<h3 id="list-ads-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bookmark|query|string|false|Cursor used to fetch the next page of items|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Maximum number of items to include in a single page.<br>See documentation on [Pagination](/docs/reference/pagination/) for more information.|
|order|query|[Pinterest.Lib.PaginationOrder](#schemapinterest.lib.paginationorder)|false|The order in which to sort the items returned: "ASCENDING" or "DESCENDING" by ID.<br>Note that higher-value IDs are associated with more-recently added items.|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|campaign_ids|query|[[CampaignIdType](#schemacampaignidtype)]|false|List of Campaign Ids to use to filter the results.|
|ad_group_ids|query|[[Pinterest.Lib.IntegerFormatType](#schemapinterest.lib.integerformattype)]|false|List of Ad group Ids to retrieve keywords from. This feature is currently in BETA and is not available to all users.|
|ad_ids|query|[[Pinterest.Lib.IntegerFormatType](#schemapinterest.lib.integerformattype)]|false|List of Ad Ids to use to filter the results.|
|entity_statuses|query|[[EntityStatus](#schemaentitystatus)]|false|Entity status|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|ASCENDING|
|order|DESCENDING|
|entity_statuses|ACTIVE|
|entity_statuses|PAUSED|
|entity_statuses|ARCHIVED|
|entity_statuses|DRAFT|
|entity_statuses|DELETED_DRAFT|

|401|Unauthorized|Authentication is required and has either failed or not been provided.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|403|Forbidden|The request was valid, but the server is refusing action. The user might not have the necessary permissions for a resource.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|404|Not Found|The requested resource could not be found on this server.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|429|Too Many Requests|The user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time and is being rate limited.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|default|Default|An unexpected error response.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|

## Get ad analytics

<a id="opIdads/analytics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/ads/analytics?start_date=1970-01-01&end_date=1970-01-01&columns=SPEND_IN_MICRO_DOLLAR&granularity=TOTAL' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/ads/analytics`

    Get analytics for the specified ads in the specified `ad_account_id`, filtered by the specified options.
    - The token's user_account must either be the Owner of the specified ad account, or have one of the necessary roles granted to them via [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts): Admin, Analyst, Campaign Manager.
    - The request must contain either ad_ids or both campaign_ids and pin_ids.
    - If granularity is not HOUR, you can pull data from up to 90 days before the current date in UTC time, with a maximum time range of 90 days.
    - If granularity is HOUR, you can pull data from up to 8 days before the current date in UTC time, with a maximum time range of 3 days.

<h3 id="get-ad-analytics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pin_ids|query|[string]|false|List of Pin IDs.|
|start_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report start date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days back from today.|
|end_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report end date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days past start_date.|
|ad_ids|query|[[Pinterest.Lib.IntegerFormatType](#schemapinterest.lib.integerformattype)]|false|List of Ad Ids to use to filter the results.|
|columns|query|[[ReportingColumnSync](#schemareportingcolumnsync)]|true|Columns to retrieve, encoded as a comma-separated string. **NOTE**: Any metrics defined as MICRO_DOLLARS returns a value based on the advertiser profile's currency field. For USD, ($1/1,000,000, or $0.000001 - one one-ten-thousandth of a cent). it's microdollars. Otherwise, it's in microunits of the advertiser's currency.<br><br>For example, if the advertiser's currency is GBP (British pound sterling), all MICRO_DOLLARS fields will be in GBP microunits (1/1,000,000 British pound).<br><br>If a column has no value, it may not be returned.|
|granularity|query|[Granularity](#schemagranularity)|true|  TOTAL - metrics are aggregated over the specified date range.<br><br>  DAY - metrics are broken down daily.<br><br>  HOUR - metrics are broken down hourly.<br><br>  WEEK - metrics are broken down weekly.<br><br>  MONTH - metrics are broken down monthly|
|click_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a pin click action. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `30` days.|
|engagement_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for an engagement action. Engagements include saves, closeups, link clicks, and carousel card swipes. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `30` days. **Note:** This parameter no longer returns new data. However, you can still access historic data through **Sept 30, 2027**.|
|view_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a view action. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `1` day.|
|conversion_report_time|query|string|false|The date by which the conversion metrics returned from this endpoint will be reported. There are two dates associated with a conversion event: the date that the user interacted with the ad, and the date that the user completed a conversion event.|
|campaign_ids|query|[[CampaignIdType](#schemacampaignidtype)]|false|List of Campaign Ids to use to filter the results.|
|reporting_timezone|query|[ReportingTimeZone](#schemareportingtimezone)|false|Specify the timezone to be applied for the reporting. This feature is currently in BETA and is not available to all users.|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

## Get targeting analytics for ads

<a id="opIdad_targeting_analytics/get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/ads/targeting_analytics?ad_ids=string&start_date=1970-01-01&end_date=1970-01-01&targeting_types=APPTYPE&columns=SPEND_IN_MICRO_DOLLAR&granularity=TOTAL' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/ads/targeting_analytics`

Get targeting analytics for one or more ads. For the requested ad(s) and metrics, the response will include the requested metric information (e.g. SPEND_IN_DOLLAR) for the requested target type (e.g. "age_bucket") for applicable values (e.g. "45-49").

* The token's user_account must either be the Owner of the specified ad account, or have one of the necessary roles granted to them via [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts): Admin, Analyst, Campaign Manager.
* If granularity is not HOUR, you can pull data from up to 90 days before the current date in UTC time, with a maximum time range of 90 days.
* If granularity is HOUR, you can pull data from up to 8 days before the current date in UTC time, with a maximum time range of 3 days.

|granularity|query|[Granularity](#schemagranularity)|true|  TOTAL - metrics are aggregated over the specified date range.<br><br>  DAY - metrics are broken down daily.<br><br>  HOUR - metrics are broken down hourly.<br><br>  WEEK - metrics are broken down weekly.<br><br>  MONTH - metrics are broken down monthly|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The request has succeeded.|[MetricsResponse](#schemametricsresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|The request could not be understood by the server due to unexpected data.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication is required and has either failed or not been provided.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|403|Forbidden|The request was valid, but the server is refusing action. The user might not have the necessary permissions for a resource.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|404|Not Found|The requested resource could not be found on this server.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|429|Too Many Requests|The user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time and is being rate limited.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|default|Default|An unexpected error response.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
pinterest_oauth2 ( Scopes: ads:read ), client_credentials ( Scopes: ads:read )
</aside>

## Get ad

<a id="opIdads/get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/ads/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/ads/{ad_id}`

Get a specific ad given the ad ID. If your pin is rejected, rejected_reasons will
contain additional information from the Ad Review process.
For more information about our policies and rejection reasons see the [Pinterest advertising standards](https://www.pinterest.com/_/_/policy/advertising-guidelines/).

<h3 id="get-ad-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_id|path|string|true|The ID of this ad.|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

## Fetch ad preview records for one or more ad groups

<a id="opIdcampaign_ad_preview/read"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/campaign_ad_preview?ad_group_ids=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/campaign_ad_preview`

Fetch ad preview records for one or more ad groups.
Returns all active previews associated with the provided ad group IDs.

<h3 id="fetch-ad-preview-records-for-one-or-more-ad-groups-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_group_ids|query|[[AdGroupIdType](#schemaadgroupidtype)]|true|List of Ad group Ids to use to filter the results.|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

> Example responses

<h1 id="pinterest-rest-api-advancedauction">advanced_auction</h1>

View, create, or update advanced auction item bid options.

## Get item bid options (POST)

<a id="opIdadvanced_auction_items_get/post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/advanced_auction/items/get \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "catalog_id": "2680059592705",
    "items": [
      {
        "country": "AD",
        "item_id": "DS0294-M",
        "language": "EN"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /advanced_auction/items/get`

Get the bid options for a batch of retail catalog items.

The catalog must be owned by the "operation user_account". [See detailed documentation here.](/docs/api-features/shopping-overview/#Update%20items%20in%20batch) By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account: `Owner`, `Admin`.

This endpoint is not available to all users.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "catalog_id": "2680059592705",
  "items": [
    {
      "country": "AD",
      "item_id": "DS0294-M",
      "language": "EN"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-item-bid-options-post-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|body|body|[AdvancedAuctionItemsGetRequest](#schemaadvancedauctionitemsgetrequest)|true|none|
|» catalog_id|body|object|true|Catalog id pertaining to the retail item|
|» items|body|[[AdvancedAuctionKey](#schemaadvancedauctionkey)]|true|A list of retail catalog items to fetch bid options for|

## Operate on item level bid options

<a id="opIdadvanced_auction_items_submit/post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/advanced_auction/items/submit \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "catalog_id": "2680059592705",
    "items": [
      {
        "item_id": "DS0294-M",
        "country": "US",
        "language": "EN",
        "operation": "UPSERT",
        "bid_options": {
          "bid_in_micro_currency": 5000000,
          "app_type_multipliers": {
            "android_mobile": 1.1,
            "android_tablet": 1.1,
            "ipad": 1.2,
            "iphone": 1.2,
            "web": 0.9,
            "web_mobile": 0.8
          }
        },
        "update_mask": [
          "BID",
          "APP_TYPE_BID_MULTIPLIER_SET"
        ],
        "errors": [
          {
            "code": 6,
            "message": "Bid in micro currency should be non-negative"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /advanced_auction/items/submit`

This endpoint supports multiple operations on a set of one or more bid options (bid price and bid adjustments for targeting categories) for retail catalog items. These advanced auction settings are applied in campaigns using objective_type `CATALOG_SALES` and ad groups using bid_strategy_type `MAX_BID`.

The catalog must be owned by the "operation user_account". [See detailed documentation here.](/docs/api-features/modify-items-in-batch/) By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account: `Owner`, `Admin`.

This endpoint is not available to all users.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "catalog_id": "2680059592705",
  "items": [
    {
      "item_id": "DS0294-M",
      "country": "US",
      "language": "EN",
      "operation": "UPSERT",

        }

      ],
      "errors": [
        {
          "code": 6,
          "message": "Bid in micro currency should be non-negative"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h1 id="pinterest-rest-api-audienceinsights">audience_insights</h1>

View audience insights.

## Get audience insights

<a id="opIdaudience_insights/get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/audience_insights?audience_insight_type=YOUR_TOTAL_AUDIENCE' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/audience_insights`

Get Audience Insights for an ad account. The response will return insights for 3 types of audiences: the ad account's engaged audience on Pinterest, the ad account's total audience on Pinterest and Pinterest's total audience.

[Learn more about Audience Insights](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/audience-insights).

<h3 id="get-audience-insights-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|audience_insight_type|query|[AudienceInsightType](#schemaaudienceinsighttype)|true|Type of audience insights.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|audience_insight_type|YOUR_TOTAL_AUDIENCE|
|audience_insight_type|YOUR_ENGAGED_AUDIENCE|
|audience_insight_type|PINTEREST_TOTAL_AUDIENCE|

## Get audience insights scope and type

<a id="opIdaudience_insights_scope_and_type/get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/insights/audiences \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/insights/audiences`

Get the scope and type of available audiences, which along with a date, is an audience that has recently had an interaction (referred to here as a type) on pins. Interacted pins can belong to at least the most common **partner** or **Pinterest** scopes. This means that user interactions made on advertiser or partner pins will have the **partner** scope. You can also have user interactions performed in general on Pinterest with the **Pinterest** scope. In that case, you can then use the returned type and scope values together on requests to other endpoints to retrieve insight metrics for a desired audience.

<h3 id="get-audience-insights-scope-and-type-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "date": "2022-10-09",
      "scope": "PARTNER",
      "type": "IMPRESSION_PLUS_ENGAGEMENT"
    }
  ]
}
```
