## Update audience sharing between ad accounts

<a id="opIdupdate_ad_account_to_ad_account_shared_audience"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/audiences/ad_accounts/shared \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "audience_id": "2542621871096",
    "operation_type": "SHARE",
    "recipient_account_ids": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/audiences/ad_accounts/shared`

From an ad account, share a specific audience with another ad account, or revoke access to a previously shared audience. Only the audience owner account can share the audience. The recipient ad account(s) must be in the same [Pinterest Business Hierarchy](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/create-and-manage-accounts) as the business owner of the ad account.

This endpoint is not available to all apps. [Learn more](/docs/getting-started/using-beta-and-restricted-features/).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "audience_id": "2542621871096",
  "operation_type": "SHARE",
  "recipient_account_ids": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-audience-sharing-between-ad-accounts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|body|body|[AdAccountToAdAccountSharedAudienceUpdateWithRequiredBody](#schemaadaccounttoadaccountsharedaudienceupdatewithrequiredbody)|true|none|
|» audience_id|body|object|true|Unique identifier of an audience|
|» operation_type|body|[OperationType](#schemaoperationtype)|true|Operation type to share a specific audience or revoke access to a previously shared audience|
|» recipient_account_ids|body|[[Pinterest.Lib.IntegerFormatType](#schemapinterest.lib.integerformattype)]|true|Ad account IDs to share with or revoke from (request) / that received the audience (response).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» operation_type|SHARE|
|» operation_type|REVOKE|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "audience_id": "2542621871096",
  "permissions": [
    "RESOURCE_PINNER_LIST_READER",
    "RESOURCE_PINNER_LIST_OWNER"
  ],
  "recipient_account_ids": [

}
```

## Update audience sharing from a business to ad accounts

<a id="opIdupdate_business_to_ad_account_shared_audience"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/businesses/string/audiences/ad_accounts/shared \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "audience_id": "2542621871096",
    "operation_type": "SHARE",
    "recipient_account_ids": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /businesses/{business_id}/audiences/ad_accounts/shared`

From a business, share a specific audience with other ad account(s), or revoke access to a previously shared audience.

- If the business is the owner of the audience, it can share with any ad account within the same business hierarchy.
- If the business is the recipient of the audience, it can share with any of its owned ad accounts.

This endpoint is not available to all apps. [Learn more](/docs/getting-started/using-beta-and-restricted-features/).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "audience_id": "2542621871096",
  "operation_type": "SHARE",
  "recipient_account_ids": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-audience-sharing-from-a-business-to-ad-accounts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

## Update audience sharing between businesses

<a id="opIdupdate_business_to_business_shared_audience"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/businesses/string/audiences/businesses/shared \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "audience_id": "2542621871096",
    "operation_type": "SHARE",
    "recipient_business_ids": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /businesses/{business_id}/audiences/businesses/shared`

From a business, share a specific audience with another business account, or revoke access to a previously shared audience. Only the audience owner can share the audience with other businesses, and the recipient business must be within the same business hierarchy.

This endpoint is not available to all apps. [Learn more](/docs/getting-started/using-beta-and-restricted-features/).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "audience_id": "2542621871096",
  "operation_type": "SHARE",
  "recipient_business_ids": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

|» recipient_business_ids|body|[[Pinterest.Lib.IntegerFormatType](#schemapinterest.lib.integerformattype)]|true|Business IDs to share with or revoke from (request) / that received the audience (response).|

## List accounts with access to an audience owned by a business

<a id="opIdbusiness_account_audiences_shared_accounts/list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/businesses/string/audiences/shared/accounts?audience_id=string&account_type=AD_ACCOUNT' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /businesses/{business_id}/audiences/shared/accounts`

List all ad accounts and/or businesses that have access to a specific audience. The audience must either be owned by an ad account in the requesting business, or it must have been shared with the requesting business. If the requesting business is not the owner of the audience, only ad accounts owned by the requesting business will be returned.

|page_size|query|integer|false|Maximum number of items to include in a single page.<br>See documentation on [Pagination](/docs/reference/pagination/) for more information.|

## Redeem ad credits

<a id="opIdads_credit/redeem"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/ads_credit/redeem \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "offerCodeHash": "138e9e0ff7e38cf511b880975eb574c09aa9d5e1657590ab0431040da68caa67",
    "validateOnly": true
  }'
```

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/ads_credit/redeem`

Redeem ads credit on behalf of the ad account id and apply it towards billing.

**This endpoint might not be available to all apps. [Learn more](/docs/getting-started/using-beta-and-restricted-features/).**

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "offerCodeHash": "138e9e0ff7e38cf511b880975eb574c09aa9d5e1657590ab0431040da68caa67",
  "validateOnly": true
}
```

<h3 id="redeem-ad-credits-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|body|body|[AdsCreditRedeemCreate](#schemaadscreditredeemcreate)|true|none|
|» offerCodeHash|body|string|true|Takes in a SHA256 hash of the offerCode.|
|» validateOnly|body|boolean|true|If true, only validate if we can redeem offer code. Otherwise it will actually apply the offer code to the account|

```bash
    "order_name": "string",
    "pmp_id": "string",
    "po_number": "string",
    "start_date": "string",
    "user_email": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/ssio/insertion_orders`

  Create insertion order through SSIO for `ad_account_id`.

```json
  "budget_amount": 0,
```

## List boards

<a id="opIdboards/list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/boards \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /boards`

Get a list of the boards owned by the "operation user_account" + group boards where this account is a collaborator
Optional: Business Access: Specify an ad_account_id to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account".
Optional: Specify a privacy type (public, protected, or secret) to indicate which boards to return.
* If no privacy is specified, all boards that can be returned (based on the scopes of the token and ad_account role if applicable) will be returned.

<h3 id="list-boards-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|privacy|query|[BoardPrivacyFilter](#schemaboardprivacyfilter)|false|The privacy level of the board|
|bookmark|query|string|false|Cursor used to fetch the next page of items|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Maximum number of items to include in a single page.<br>See documentation on [Pagination](/docs/reference/pagination/) for more information.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|privacy|ALL|
|privacy|PUBLIC|
|privacy|PROTECTED|
|privacy|SECRET|
|privacy|PUBLIC_AND_SECRET|

## Create board

<a id="opIdboards/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/boards \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "My favorite summer recipes",
    "is_ads_only": true,
    "name": "Summer recipes",
    "privacy": "PUBLIC"
  }'
```

`POST /boards`

Create a board owned by the "operation user_account".
Optional: Business Access: Specify an ad_account_id to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account".
* By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "My favorite summer recipes",
  "is_ads_only": true,
  "name": "Summer recipes",
  "privacy": "PUBLIC"
}
```

<h3 id="create-board-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|body|body|[BoardCreate](#schemaboardcreate)|true|none|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» is_ads_only|body|boolean|false|If set to `true`, the board will be ad-only and can store ad-only Pins.|
|» name|body|string|true|    Name of the board.<br><br>    **Note:** If you create an ad-only board by setting `is_ads_only`<br>    to `true`, the board name automatically becomes "Ad-only Pins".|
|» privacy|body|object|false|    Privacy setting for a board. Learn more about [secret](https://help.pinterest.com/en/article/secret-boards)<br>    boards and [protected](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/protected-boards) boards.<br><br>    **Note:** If you create an ad-only board by setting `is_ads_only`<br>    to `true`, the `privacy` settng automatically becomes `PROTECTED`. |

## Get advertiser entities in bulk

<a id="opIdbulk_download/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/bulk/download \
  -X POST \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "campaign_filter": {
      "campaign_status": [
        "RUNNING"
      ],

      "objective_type": [
        "AWARENESS"
      ],
      "start_time": "1622848072"
    },
    "entity_ids": [
      "string"
    ],
    "entity_types": [
      "CAMPAIGN",
      "AD_GROUP"
    ],
    "output_format": "JSON",
    "updated_since": "1622848072"
  }'
```

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/bulk/download`

Create an asynchronous report that may include information on campaigns, ad groups, product groups, ads,
keywords, schedules,and/or labels; can filter by campaigns. Though the entities may be active, archived, or paused,
only active entities will return data.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "campaign_filter": {
    "campaign_status": [
      "RUNNING"
    ],
    "end_time": "1622848072",
    "name": "campaign name",
    "objective_type": [
      "AWARENESS"
    ],
    "start_time": "1622848072"
  },
  "entity_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "entity_types": [
    "CAMPAIGN",
    "AD_GROUP"
  ],
  "output_format": "JSON",
  "updated_since": "1622848072"
}
```

<h3 id="get-advertiser-entities-in-bulk-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|body|body|[BulkDownloadCreate](#schemabulkdownloadcreate)|true|none|
|» campaign_filter|body|[BulkDownloadCampaignFilter](#schemabulkdownloadcampaignfilter)|false|none|
|» entity_ids|body|[[BulkDownloadEntityIdsItems](#schemabulkdownloadentityidsitems)]|false|All entities specified by these IDs as well as their children and grandchildren will be downloaded if the entity type is one of the types requested to be downloaded.|
|» entity_types|body|[[BulkEntityType](#schemabulkentitytype)]|false|All entity types specified will be downloaded. Fewer types result in faster downloads.|
|» output_format|body|object|false|none|
|» updated_since|body|string|false|Unix UTC timestamp to retrieve all entities that have changed since this time.|

|» entity_types|AD_GROUP|

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/bulk/upsert`

Either create or update any combination of campaigns, ad groups, product groups, ads, keywords, schedules, or labels.
Note that this request will be processed asynchronously; the response will include a <code>request_id</code>
that can be used to obtain the status of the request.

|» create|body|[BulkUpsertRequestCreate](#schemabulkupsertrequestcreate)|false|Request for creation of entities in bulk.|
|» update|body|[BulkUpsertRequestUpdate](#schemabulkupsertrequestupdate)|false|Request for creation of entities in bulk.|

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
pinterest_oauth2 ( Scopes: ads:write )
</aside>

## Download advertiser entities in bulk

<a id="opIdbulk_request/get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/bulk/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/bulk/{bulk_request_id}`

Get the status of a bulk request by `request_id`, along with a download URL that will allow you to download the
new or updated entity data (campaigns, ad groups, product groups, ads, schedules, or keywords).

<h3 id="download-advertiser-entities-in-bulk-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|bulk_request_id|path|string|true|Bulk request ID that is from one of the entities bulk endpoints|
|include_details|query|boolean|false|If set to True then attach the errors/details to all the requests|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result_url": "string",
  "status": "RUNNING",
  "workload_id": 0
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

<h3 id="download-advertiser-entities-in-bulk-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The request has succeeded.|[BulkJobData](#schemabulkjobdata)|
|400|Bad Request|The request could not be understood by the server due to unexpected data.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication is required and has either failed or not been provided.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|403|Forbidden|The request was valid, but the server is refusing action. The user might not have the necessary permissions for a resource.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|404|Not Found|The requested resource could not be found on this server.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|429|Too Many Requests|The user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time and is being rate limited.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|default|Default|An unexpected error response.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
pinterest_oauth2 ( Scopes: ads:read ), client_credentials ( Scopes: ads:read )
</aside>

<h1 id="pinterest-rest-api-campaigns">campaigns</h1>

View, create or update campaigns.

## List campaigns

<a id="opIdcampaigns/list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/campaigns \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/campaigns`

Get a list of the campaigns in the specified `ad_account_id`, filtered by the specified options.
- The token's user_account must either be the Owner of the specified ad account, or have one of the necessary
roles granted to them via [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts): Admin, Analyst, Campaign Manager.

<h3 id="list-campaigns-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bookmark|query|string|false|Cursor used to fetch the next page of items|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Maximum number of items to include in a single page.<br>See documentation on [Pagination](/docs/reference/pagination/) for more information.|
|order|query|[Pinterest.Lib.PaginationOrder](#schemapinterest.lib.paginationorder)|false|The order in which to sort the items returned: "ASCENDING" or "DESCENDING" by ID.<br>Note that higher-value IDs are associated with more-recently added items.|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|campaign_ids|query|[[CampaignIdType](#schemacampaignidtype)]|false|List of Campaign Ids to use to filter the results.|
|entity_statuses|query|[[EntityStatus](#schemaentitystatus)]|false|Entity status|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|ASCENDING|
|order|DESCENDING|
|entity_statuses|ACTIVE|
|entity_statuses|PAUSED|
|entity_statuses|ARCHIVED|
|entity_statuses|DRAFT|
|entity_statuses|DELETED_DRAFT|

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/campaigns`

Create multiple new campaigns. Every campaign has its own campaign_id
and houses one or more ad groups, which contain one or more ads.

For more, see [Set up your campaign](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/set-up-your-campaign/).

**Note:**
- The values for `lifetime_spend_cap` and `daily_spend_cap` are microcurrency amounts based on the currency field set in the advertiser's profile (e.g. USD).

Microcurrency is used to track very small transactions, based on the currency set in the advertiser's profile.

A microcurrency unit is 10^(-6) of the standard unit of currency selected in the advertiser's profile.

**Equivalency equations**, using dollars as an example currency:

- $1 = 1,000,000 microdollars
- 1 microdollar = $0.000001

**To convert between currency and microcurrency**, using dollars as an example currency:

- To convert dollars to microdollars, multiply dollars by 1,000,000
- To convert microdollars to dollars, divide microdollars by 1,000,000

## Get campaign analytics

<a id="opIdcampaigns/analytics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/campaigns/analytics?start_date=1970-01-01&end_date=1970-01-01&campaign_ids=string&columns=SPEND_IN_MICRO_DOLLAR&granularity=TOTAL' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/campaigns/analytics`

Get analytics for the specified campaigns in the specified `ad_account_id`, filtered by the specified options.
- The token's user_account must either be the Owner of the specified ad account, or have one of the necessary roles granted to them via [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts): Admin, Analyst, Campaign Manager.
- If granularity is not HOUR, you can pull data from up to 90 days before the current date in UTC time, with a maximum time range of 90 days.
- If granularity is HOUR, you can pull data from up to 8 days before the current date in UTC time, with a maximum time range of 3 days.

<h3 id="get-campaign-analytics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report start date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days back from today.|
|end_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report end date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days past start_date.|
|campaign_ids|query|[[CampaignIdRequiredType](#schemacampaignidrequiredtype)]|true|List of Campaign Ids to use to filter the results.|
|columns|query|[[ReportingColumnSync](#schemareportingcolumnsync)]|true|Columns to retrieve, encoded as a comma-separated string. **NOTE**: Any metrics defined as MICRO_DOLLARS returns a value based on the advertiser profile's currency field. For USD, ($1/1,000,000, or $0.000001 - one one-ten-thousandth of a cent). it's microdollars. Otherwise, it's in microunits of the advertiser's currency.<br><br>For example, if the advertiser's currency is GBP (British pound sterling), all MICRO_DOLLARS fields will be in GBP microunits (1/1,000,000 British pound).<br><br>If a column has no value, it may not be returned.|
|granularity|query|[Granularity](#schemagranularity)|true|  TOTAL - metrics are aggregated over the specified date range.<br><br>  DAY - metrics are broken down daily.<br><br>  HOUR - metrics are broken down hourly.<br><br>  WEEK - metrics are broken down weekly.<br><br>  MONTH - metrics are broken down monthly|
|click_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a pin click action. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `30` days.|
|engagement_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for an engagement action. Engagements include saves, closeups, link clicks, and carousel card swipes. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `30` days. **Note:** This parameter no longer returns new data. However, you can still access historic data through **Sept 30, 2027**.|
|view_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a view action. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `1` day.|
|conversion_report_time|query|string|false|The date by which the conversion metrics returned from this endpoint will be reported. There are two dates associated with a conversion event: the date that the user interacted with the ad, and the date that the user completed a conversion event.|
|aggregate_report_rows|query|boolean|false|Determines if report rows should be aggregated across all requested entities. This feature is currently in BETA and is not available to all users.|
|reporting_timezone|query|[ReportingTimeZone](#schemareportingtimezone)|false|Specify the timezone to be applied for the reporting. This feature is currently in BETA and is not available to all users.|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

## Get targeting analytics for campaigns

<a id="opIdcampaign_targeting_analytics/get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/campaigns/targeting_analytics?campaign_ids=string&start_date=1970-01-01&end_date=1970-01-01&targeting_types=APPTYPE&columns=SPEND_IN_MICRO_DOLLAR&granularity=TOTAL' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/campaigns/targeting_analytics`

Get targeting analytics for one or more campaigns. For the requested account and metrics, the response will include the requested metric information (e.g. SPEND_IN_DOLLAR) for the requested target type (e.g. "age_bucket") for applicable values (e.g. "45-49").

* The token's user_account must either be the Owner of the specified ad account, or have one of the necessary roles granted to them via [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts): Admin, Analyst, Campaign Manager.
* If granularity is not HOUR, you can pull data from up to 90 days before the current date in UTC time, with a maximum time range of 90 days.
* If granularity is HOUR, you can pull data from up to 8 days before the current date in UTC time, with a maximum time range of 3 days.

<h3 id="get-targeting-analytics-for-campaigns-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|campaign_ids|query|[[CampaignIdRequiredType](#schemacampaignidrequiredtype)]|true|List of Campaign Ids to use to filter the results.|
|start_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report start date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days back from today.|
|end_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report end date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days past start_date.|
|targeting_types|query|[[AdsAnalyticsCampaignTargetingType](#schemaadsanalyticscampaigntargetingtype)]|true|Targeting type breakdowns for the report. The reporting per targeting type is independent from each other. ["AGE_BUCKET_AND_GENDER"] is in BETA and not yet available to all users.|
|columns|query|[[ReportingColumnSync](#schemareportingcolumnsync)]|true|Columns to retrieve, encoded as a comma-separated string. **NOTE**: Any metrics defined as MICRO_DOLLARS returns a value based on the advertiser profile's currency field. For USD, ($1/1,000,000, or $0.000001 - one one-ten-thousandth of a cent). it's microdollars. Otherwise, it's in microunits of the advertiser's currency.<br><br>For example, if the advertiser's currency is GBP (British pound sterling), all MICRO_DOLLARS fields will be in GBP microunits (1/1,000,000 British pound).<br><br>If a column has no value, it may not be returned.|
|granularity|query|[Granularity](#schemagranularity)|true|  TOTAL - metrics are aggregated over the specified date range.<br><br>  DAY - metrics are broken down daily.<br><br>  HOUR - metrics are broken down hourly.<br><br>  WEEK - metrics are broken down weekly.<br><br>  MONTH - metrics are broken down monthly|
|click_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a pin click action. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `30` days.|
|engagement_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for an engagement action. Engagements include saves, closeups, link clicks, and carousel card swipes. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `30` days. **Note:** This parameter no longer returns new data. However, you can still access historic data through **Sept 30, 2027**.|
|view_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a view action. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `1` day.|
|conversion_report_time|query|string|false|The date by which the conversion metrics returned from this endpoint will be reported. There are two dates associated with a conversion event: the date that the user interacted with the ad, and the date that the user completed a conversion event.|
|attribution_types|query|[[ConversionReportAttributionType](#schemaconversionreportattributiontype)]|false|List of types of attribution for the conversion report|
|reporting_timezone|query|[ReportingTimeZone](#schemareportingtimezone)|false|Specify the timezone to be applied for the reporting. This feature is currently in BETA and is not available to all users.|

<h3 id="get-targeting-analytics-for-campaigns-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The request has succeeded.|[MetricsResponse](#schemametricsresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|The request could not be understood by the server due to unexpected data.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication is required and has either failed or not been provided.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|403|Forbidden|The request was valid, but the server is refusing action. The user might not have the necessary permissions for a resource.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|404|Not Found|The requested resource could not be found on this server.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|429|Too Many Requests|The user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time and is being rate limited.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|default|Default|An unexpected error response.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
pinterest_oauth2 ( Scopes: ads:read ), client_credentials ( Scopes: ads:read )
</aside>

## Get campaign

<a id="opIdcampaigns/get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/campaigns/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/campaigns/{campaign_id}`

Get a specific campaign given the campaign ID.

<h3 id="get-campaign-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|campaign_id|path|string|true|Campaign ID, must be associated with the ad account ID provided in the path.|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

## Get pins analytics

<a id="opIdad_pins/analytics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/pins/analytics?campaign_id=string&pin_ids=string&start_date=1970-01-01&end_date=1970-01-01&columns=SPEND_IN_MICRO_DOLLAR&granularity=TOTAL' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/pins/analytics`

Get analytics for the pins given a campaign and pins in the specified `ad_account_id`, filtered by the specified options.
- The token's user_account must either be the Owner of the specified ad account, or have one of the necessary roles granted to them via [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts): Admin, Analyst, Campaign Manager.
- If granularity is not HOUR, the furthest back you can are allowed to pull data is 90 days before the current date in UTC time and the max time range supported is 90 days.
- If granularity is HOUR, the furthest back you can are allowed to pull data is 8 days before the current date in UTC time and the max time range supported is 3 days. Data will not be provided for conversion metrics but will be available for non-conversion metrics.

<h3 id="get-pins-analytics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|campaign_id|query|string|true|Campaign Id to use to filter the results.|
|pin_ids|query|[[Pinterest.Lib.IntegerFormatType](#schemapinterest.lib.integerformattype)]|true|List of Pin IDs.|
|start_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report start date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days back from today.|
|end_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report end date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days past start_date.|
|columns|query|[[ReportingColumnSync](#schemareportingcolumnsync)]|true|Columns to retrieve, encoded as a comma-separated string. **NOTE**: Any metrics defined as MICRO_DOLLARS returns a value based on the advertiser profile's currency field. For USD, ($1/1,000,000, or $0.000001 - one one-ten-thousandth of a cent). it's microdollars. Otherwise, it's in microunits of the advertiser's currency.<br><br>For example, if the advertiser's currency is GBP (British pound sterling), all MICRO_DOLLARS fields will be in GBP microunits (1/1,000,000 British pound).<br><br>If a column has no value, it may not be returned.|
|granularity|query|[Granularity](#schemagranularity)|true|  TOTAL - metrics are aggregated over the specified date range.<br><br>  DAY - metrics are broken down daily.<br><br>  HOUR - metrics are broken down hourly.<br><br>  WEEK - metrics are broken down weekly.<br><br>  MONTH - metrics are broken down monthly|
|click_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a pin click action. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `30` days.|
|engagement_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for an engagement action. Engagements include saves, closeups, link clicks, and carousel card swipes. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `30` days. **Note:** This parameter no longer returns new data. However, you can still access historic data through **Sept 30, 2027**.|
|view_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a view action. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `1` day.|
|conversion_report_time|query|string|false|The date by which the conversion metrics returned from this endpoint will be reported. There are two dates associated with a conversion event: the date that the user interacted with the ad, and the date that the user completed a conversion event.|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

<h1 id="pinterest-rest-api-catalogfeeds">catalog_feeds</h1>

View and manage catalog feeds.

## List feeds

<a id="opIdfeeds/list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/catalogs/feeds \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /catalogs/feeds`

Fetch feeds owned by the "operation user_account".
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account: Owner, Admin, Catalogs Manager.

For Retail partners, refer to [Before you get started with Catalogs](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/before-you-get-started-with-catalogs). For Hotel partners, refer to [Pinterest API for shopping](/docs/api-features/shopping-overview/).

<h3 id="list-feeds-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|catalog_id|query|string|false|Filter entities for a given catalog_id. If not given, all catalogs are considered.|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|bookmark|query|string|false|Cursor used to fetch the next page of items|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Maximum number of items to include in a single page.<br>See documentation on [Pagination](/docs/reference/pagination/) for more information.|

## Create feed

<a id="opIdfeeds/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/catalogs/feeds \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "catalog_id": "string",
    "catalog_type": "RETAIL",
    "credentials": {
      "password": "password",
      "username": "string"
    },
    "default_availability": "IN_STOCK",
    "default_country": "AD",
    "default_currency": "AED",
    "default_locale": "af-ZA",
    "format": "TSV",
    "location": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "preferred_processing_schedule": {
      "time": "string",
      "timezone": {}
    },
    "status": "ACTIVE"
  }'
```

`POST /catalogs/feeds`

Create a new feed owned by the "operation user_account".
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Please, be aware that "default_country"
and "default_locale" are not required in the spec for forward compatibility
but for now the API will not accept requests without those fields.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account: Owner, Admin, Catalogs Manager.

For Retail partners, refer to [Before you get started with Catalogs](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/before-you-get-started-with-catalogs). For Hotel partners, refer to [Pinterest API for shopping](/docs/api-features/shopping-overview/).

Note: Access to the Creative Assets catalog type is restricted to a specific group of users.
If you require access, please reach out to your partner manager.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "catalog_id": "string",
  "catalog_type": "RETAIL",
  "credentials": {
    "password": "password",
    "username": "string"
  },
  "default_availability": "IN_STOCK",
  "default_country": "AD",
  "default_currency": "AED",
  "default_locale": "af-ZA",
  "format": "TSV",
  "location": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "preferred_processing_schedule": {
    "time": "string",
    "timezone": {}
  },
  "status": "ACTIVE"
}
```

<h3 id="create-feed-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|body|body|[CatalogsFeedCreateRequestSchema](#schemacatalogsfeedcreaterequestschema)|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[CatalogsVerticalFeedsCreateRequest](#schemacatalogsverticalfeedscreaterequest)|false|Request object for creating a feed.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[CatalogsFeedsCreateRequest](#schemacatalogsfeedscreaterequest)|false|Request object for creating a feed. Please, be aware that "default_country" and "default_locale" are not required in the spec for forward compatibility but for now the API will not accept requests without those fields.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response


`PATCH /catalogs/feeds/{feed_id}`

Update a feed owned by the "operation user_account".
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account: Owner, Admin, Catalogs Manager.

## List feed processing results

<a id="opIdfeed_processing_results/list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/catalogs/feeds/string/processing_results \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /catalogs/feeds/{feed_id}/processing_results`

Fetch a feed processing results owned by the "operation user_account". Please note that for now the bookmark parameter is not functional and only the first page will be available until it is implemented in some release in the near future.
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account: Owner, Admin, Catalogs Manager.

[Learn more](/docs/api-features/shopping-overview/)

<h3 id="list-feed-processing-results-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|feed_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of a feed.|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|bookmark|query|string|false|Cursor used to fetch the next page of items|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Maximum number of items to include in a single page.<br>See documentation on [Pagination](/docs/reference/pagination/) for more information.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The request has succeeded.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|The request could not be understood by the server due to unexpected data.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication is required and has either failed or not been provided.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|403|Forbidden|The request was valid, but the server is refusing action. The user might not have the necessary permissions for a resource.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|404|Not Found|The requested resource could not be found on this server.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|

|default|Default|An unexpected error response.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|

<h3 id="list-feed-processing-results-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bookmark|string \| null|false|none|none|
|items|[[CatalogsFeedProcessingResult](#schemacatalogsfeedprocessingresult)]|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
pinterest_oauth2 ( Scopes: catalogs:read )
</aside>

## List item issues

<a id="opIditems_issues/list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/catalogs/processing_results/string/item_issues \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /catalogs/processing_results/{processing_result_id}/item_issues`

List item validation issues for a given feed processing result owned by the "operation user_account". Up to 20 random samples of affected items are returned for each error and warning code. Please note that for now query parameters 'item_numbers' and 'item_validation_issue' cannot be used simultaneously until it is implemented in some release in the future.
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account: Owner, Admin, Catalogs Manager.

Note: To get a list of all affected items instead of sampled issues, please refer to [Build catalogs report](/docs/api/v5/#operation/reports/create) and [Get catalogs report](/docs/api/v5/#operation/reports/get) endpoints. Moreover, they support multiple types of catalogs.

[Learn more](/docs/api-features/shopping-overview/)

<h3 id="list-item-issues-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|processing_result_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of a feed processing result. It can be acquired from the "id" field of the "items" array within the response of the [List processing results for a given feed](/docs/api/v5/#operation/feed_processing_results/list).|
|item_numbers|query|[integer]|false|Item number based on order of appearance in the Catalogs Feed. For example, '0' refers to first item found in a feed that was downloaded from a 'location' specified during feed creation.|
|item_validation_issue|query|[CatalogsItemValidationIssue](#schemacatalogsitemvalidationissue)|false|Filter item validation issues that have a given type of item validation issue.|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|bookmark|query|string|false|Cursor used to fetch the next page of items|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Maximum number of items to include in a single page.<br>See documentation on [Pagination](/docs/reference/pagination/) for more information.|

<h3 id="list-item-issues-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The request has succeeded.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|The request could not be understood by the server due to unexpected data.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication is required and has either failed or not been provided.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|403|Forbidden|The request was valid, but the server is refusing action. The user might not have the necessary permissions for a resource.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|404|Not Found|The requested resource could not be found on this server.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|429|Too Many Requests|The user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time and is being rate limited.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|default|Default|An unexpected error response.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bookmark|string \| null|false|none|none|
|items|[[CatalogsItemValidationIssues](#schemacatalogsitemvalidationissues)]|true|none|none|

pinterest_oauth2 ( Scopes: catalogs:read )
</aside>

<h1 id="pinterest-rest-api-catalogitems">catalog_items</h1>

View and manage catalog items directly without a feed.

## Get catalogs items (POST)

<a id="opIditems/post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/catalogs/items \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "country": "AD",
    "filters": {
      "catalog_id": "string",
      "catalog_type": "RETAIL",
      "item_ids": [
        "string"
      ]
    },
    "language": "af-ZA"
  }'
```

`POST /catalogs/items`

Get the items of the catalog owned by the "operation user_account". [See detailed documentation here.](/docs/api-features/shopping-overview/#Update%20items%20in%20batch)
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account: Owner, Admin, Catalogs Manager.

Note: Access to the Creative Assets catalog type is restricted to a specific group of users.
If you require access, please reach out to your partner manager.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "country": "AD",
  "filters": {
    "catalog_id": "string",
    "catalog_type": "RETAIL",
    "item_ids": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "language": "af-ZA"
}
```

<h3 id="get-catalogs-items-post-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|body|body|[CatalogsItemsRequest](#schemacatalogsitemsrequest)|true|none|
|» country|body|[Country](#schemacountry)|true|Country ID from ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.|
|» filters|body|[CatalogsItemsPostFilters](#schemacatalogsitemspostfilters)|true|none|
|» language|body|[CatalogsLocale](#schemacatalogslocale) \| [Language](#schemalanguage)|true|We recommend using the CatalogsLocale values.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[CatalogsLocale](#schemacatalogslocale)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[Language](#schemalanguage)|false|Language code, which is among the official ISO 639-1 language list.|

<h3 id="get-catalogs-items-post-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The request has succeeded.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|The request could not be understood by the server due to unexpected data.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication is required and has either failed or not been provided.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|403|Forbidden|The request was valid, but the server is refusing action. The user might not have the necessary permissions for a resource.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|404|Not Found|The requested resource could not be found on this server.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|429|Too Many Requests|The user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time and is being rate limited.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|
|default|Default|An unexpected error response.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|

<h3 id="get-catalogs-items-post-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|items|[[ItemResponse](#schemaitemresponse)]|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
pinterest_oauth2 ( Scopes: catalogs:read )
</aside>

`POST /catalogs/items/batch`

This endpoint supports multiple operations on a set of one or more catalog items owned by the "operation user_account". [See detailed documentation here.](/docs/work-with-catalogs/modify-items-in-batch/)
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account: Owner, Admin, Catalogs Manager.

Note:
- Access to the Creative Assets catalog type is restricted to a specific group of users.
If you require access, please reach out to your partner manager.
- The item UPSERT operation is restricted to users without a feed data source. If you plan to migrate item ingestion from feeds to the API, please reach out to your partner manager or via the Help Center to get assistance.

## Get item batch status

<a id="opIditems_batch/get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/catalogs/items/batch/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /catalogs/items/batch/{batch_id}`

Get a single catalogs items batch owned by the "operating user_account". [See detailed documentation here.](/docs/api-features/shopping-overview/#Update%20items%20in%20batch)
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account: Owner, Admin, Catalogs Manager.

|batch_id|path|[Pinterest.Lib.IntegerFormatType](#schemapinterest.lib.integerformattype)|true|Id of a catalogs items batch to fetch|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

<h1 id="pinterest-rest-api-catalogproductgroups">catalog_product_groups</h1>

View and manage catalog product groups using filters.

## List product groups

<a id="opIdcatalogs_product_groups/list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/catalogs/product_groups \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /catalogs/product_groups`

Get a list of product groups for a given Catalogs Feed Id owned by the "operation user_account".
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account: Owner, Admin, Catalogs Manager.

[Learn more](/docs/api-features/shopping-overview/)

<h3 id="list-product-groups-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|query|[integer]|false|Comma-separated list of product group ids|
|feed_id|query|string|false|Filter entities for a given feed_id. If not given, all feeds are considered.|
|catalog_id|query|string|false|Filter entities for a given catalog_id. If not given, all catalogs are considered.|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|bookmark|query|string|false|Cursor used to fetch the next page of items|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Maximum number of items to include in a single page.<br>See documentation on [Pagination](/docs/reference/pagination/) for more information.|

> 200 Response

## Create product group

<a id="opIdcatalogs_product_groups/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/catalogs/product_groups \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "string",
    "feed_id": "2680059592705",
    "filters": {
      "any_of": [
        {
          "MIN_PRICE": {
            "inclusion": true,
            "negated": true,
            "values": 0
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    "is_featured": true,
    "name": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /catalogs/product_groups`

Create product group to use in Catalogs owned by the "operation user_account".
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account: Owner, Admin, Catalogs Manager.
"Catalog-based product groups" can include items from all data sources (feeds and API) and are available to both non-retail catalogs with any data sources and retail catalogs with API-created items. If your catalog only contains retail items created via feeds, you should use the "retail feed-based" option.
[Learn more](/docs/api-features/shopping-overview/)

Note: Access to the Creative Assets catalog type is restricted to a specific group of users.
If you require access, please reach out to your partner manager.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "feed_id": "2680059592705",
  "filters": {
    "any_of": [
      {
        "MIN_PRICE": {
          "inclusion": true,
          "negated": true,
          "values": 0
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "is_featured": true,
  "name": "string"
}
```

## Update single product group

<a id="opIdcatalogs_product_groups/update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/catalogs/product_groups/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "string",
    "filters": {
      "any_of": [
        {
          "MIN_PRICE": {
            "inclusion": true,
            "negated": true,
            "values": 0
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    "is_featured": true,
    "name": "string"
  }'
```

`PATCH /catalogs/product_groups/{product_group_id}`

Update product group owned by the "operation user_account" to use in Catalogs.
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account: Owner, Admin, Catalogs Manager.
"Catalog-based product groups" can include items from all data sources (feeds and API) and are available to both non-retail catalogs with any data sources and retail catalogs with API-created items. If your catalog only contains retail items created via feeds, you should use the "retail feed-based" option.
[Learn more](/docs/api-features/shopping-overview/)

Note: Access to the Creative Assets catalog type is restricted to a specific group of users.
If you require access, please reach out to your partner manager.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "filters": {
    "any_of": [
      {
        "MIN_PRICE": {
          "inclusion": true,
          "negated": true,
          "values": 0
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "is_featured": true,
  "name": "string"
}
```

|» *oneOf*|body|[CatalogsProductGroupUpdateRequest](#schemacatalogsproductgroupupdaterequest)|false|Request object for updating a product group.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[CatalogsVerticalProductGroupUpdateRequest](#schemacatalogsverticalproductgroupupdaterequest)|false|Request object for updating a catalog based product group.|

## List products by filter

<a id="opIdproducts_by_product_group_filter/list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/catalogs/products/get_by_product_group_filters \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "feed_id": "2680059592705",
    "filters": {
      "any_of": [
        {
          "MIN_PRICE": {
            "inclusion": true,
            "negated": true,
            "values": 0
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /catalogs/products/get_by_product_group_filters`

List products Pins owned by the "operation user_account" that meet the criteria specified in the Catalogs Product Group Filter given in the request.
- This endpoint has been implemented in POST to allow for complex filters. This specific POST endpoint is designed to be idempotent.
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account: Owner, Admin, Catalogs Manager.

Note: This endpoint only supports RETAIL catalog at the moment.

[Learn more](/docs/api-features/shopping-overview/)

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "feed_id": "2680059592705",
  "filters": {
    "any_of": [
      {
        "MIN_PRICE": {
          "inclusion": true,
          "negated": true,
          "values": 0
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="list-products-by-filter-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|bookmark|query|string|false|Cursor used to fetch the next page of items|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Maximum number of items to include in a single page.<br>See documentation on [Pagination](/docs/reference/pagination/) for more information.|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|pin_metrics|query|boolean|false|Specify whether to return 90d and lifetime Pin metrics. Total comments<br>and total reactions are only available with lifetime Pin metrics. If Pin was<br>created before `2023-03-20` lifetime metrics will only be available<br>for Video and Idea Pin formats. Lifetime metrics are available for all Pin<br>formats since then.|

|» *oneOf*|body|[CatalogsListProductsByFeedBasedFilter](#schemacatalogslistproductsbyfeedbasedfilter)|false|Request object to list products for a given feed_id and product group filter.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[CatalogsVerticalsListProductsByCatalogBasedFilterRequest](#schemacatalogsverticalslistproductsbycatalogbasedfilterrequest)|false|Request object to list products for a given catalog_id and product group filter.|

## Build catalogs report

<a id="opIdreports/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/catalogs/reports \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "catalog_type": "RETAIL",
    "report": {
      "feed_id": "string",
      "processing_result_id": "string",
      "report_type": "FEED_INGESTION_ISSUES"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /catalogs/reports`

Async request to create a report of the catalog owned by the "operation user_account". This endpoint generates a report upon receiving the first approved request of the day. Any following requests with identical parameters will yield the same report even if data has changed.
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account: Owner, Admin, Catalogs Manager.

Note: The All Items report is limited to 25 million items per catalog.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "catalog_type": "RETAIL",
  "report": {
    "feed_id": "string",
    "processing_result_id": "string",
    "report_type": "FEED_INGESTION_ISSUES"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="build-catalogs-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|body|body|[CatalogsReportParameters](#schemacatalogsreportparameters)|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[CatalogsRetailReportParameters](#schemacatalogsretailreportparameters)|false|Parameters for retail report|
|» *oneOf*|body|[CatalogsHotelReportParameters](#schemacatalogshotelreportparameters)|false|Parameters for hotel report|

## Operate on local inventory item batch

<a id="opIdcatalogs_local_inventory_items_batch/operate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/catalogs/string/local_inventory_items/batch \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "operations": [
      {
        "attributes": {
          "ad_link": "https://examplelink.com",
          "availability": "in stock",
          "price": "49.99 USD",
          "sale_price": "24.99 USD"
        },
        "item_id": "item_id_1",
        "operation": "CREATE",
        "store_code": "store_1"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /catalogs/{catalog_id}/local_inventory_items/batch`

Managing local inventory information in batches supporting CREATE, UPDATE, UPSERT, DELETE operations.
Up to 1000 items per request to match catalogs/items.

- Must provide both item_id and store_code to identify a local inventory item.

- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an ad_account_id (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account: Owner, Admin, Catalogs Manager.

[Learn more](/docs/api-features/shopping-overview/)

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "operations": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "ad_link": "https://examplelink.com",
        "availability": "in stock",
        "price": "49.99 USD",
        "sale_price": "24.99 USD"
      },
      "item_id": "item_id_1",
      "operation": "CREATE",
      "store_code": "store_1"
    }
  ]
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|catalog_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of a catalog.|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|body|body|[LocalInventoryItemsBatchCreate](#schemalocalinventoryitemsbatchcreate)|true|none|
|» operations|body|[[LocalInventoryOperation](#schemalocalinventoryoperation)]|true|Array of inventory operations. Up to 1000 items per request.|

## Get local inventory items (POST)

<a id="opIdcatalogs_local_inventory_items/post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/catalogs/string/local_inventory_items/query \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "item_filters": [
      {
        "item_id": "item_id_1",
        "store_code": "store_1"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /catalogs/{catalog_id}/local_inventory_items/query`

Get local inventory items for a catalog owned by the "operation user_account".

- Must provide an array of {item_id, store_code} pairs in item filters to identify local inventory items.

- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an ad_account_id (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account: Owner, Admin, Catalogs Manager.

[Learn more](/docs/api-features/shopping-overview/)

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "item_filters": [
    {
      "item_id": "item_id_1",
      "store_code": "store_1"
    }
  ]
}
```

|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

## Get supplemental items batch status

## Create catalog

<a id="opIdcatalogs/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/catalogs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "catalog_type": "RETAIL",
    "name": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /catalogs`

Create a new catalog owned by the "operation user_account".
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an ad_account_id (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account: Owner, Admin, Catalogs Manager.

[Learn more](/docs/api-features/shopping-overview/)

Note: Access to the Product and Creative Assets catalog type is restricted to a specific group of users. If you require access, please reach out to your partner manager.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "catalog_type": "RETAIL",
  "name": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-catalog-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|body|body|[CatalogCreate](#schemacatalogcreate)|true|none|
|» catalog_type|body|[CatalogsType](#schemacatalogstype)|true|Type of the catalog entity.|
|» name|body|string|true|A human-friendly name associated to a catalog entity.|

#### Enumerated Values

## List available filter values

<a id="opIdcatalogs/available_filter_values"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/catalogs/available_filter_values?catalog_id=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /catalogs/available_filter_values`

Get the available filter attributes and values associated with a given feed or catalog owned by the "operation user_account".
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.
- `country`, `language`, and `feed_id` are only used in retail catalogs.
- Note: It is not guaranteed that all available filter values will be returned. Instead this endpoint will return values from a sample of up to 1000 items.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account: Owner, Admin, Catalogs Manager.

[Learn more](/docs/api-features/shopping-overview/)

<h3 id="list-available-filter-values-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|catalog_id|query|string|true|Filter entities for a given catalog_id.|
|feed_id|query|string|false|Filter entities for a given feed_id. If not given, all feeds are considered.|
|country|query|[Country](#schemacountry)|false|Country for the Catalogs Items|
|language|query|[CatalogsLocale](#schemacatalogslocale)|false|Language for the Catalogs Items|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

## Create a conversion deletion request

<a id="opIdconversion_deletion_request/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/conversion_deletion_requests \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "deletion_targets": {
      "user_emails": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/conversion_deletion_requests`

**This endpoint is currently in beta and not available to all apps.**
[Learn more](/docs/key-concepts/using-beta-and-restricted-features/).
Create a request to delete conversion data for a list of user emails and/or EPIKs, limited to the specified `ad_account_id`.
After 72 hours the request is processed and submitted to our deletion process. Then the deletion process ensures deletion
within a 30 days period, once the request is submitted to the deletion process it cannot be canceled.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "deletion_targets": {
    "user_emails": [
      "string"
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-conversion-deletion-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|body|body|[ConversionDeletionRequestCreate](#schemaconversiondeletionrequestcreate)|true|none|
|» deletion_targets|body|object|true|Object containing the targets of the conversion deletion request. Users can be identified with user_emails, epiks, or both within the same request.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[ConversionDeletionRequestUserEmailTargets](#schemaconversiondeletionrequestuseremailtargets)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[ConversionDeletionRequestEPIKTargets](#schemaconversiondeletionrequestepiktargets)|false|none|

```json
}
```

<h1 id="pinterest-rest-api-conversioneqs">conversion_eqs</h1>

Get the Event Quality Score (EQS) of your conversion signals.

## Get event quality score (EQS)

<a id="opIdconversion_eqs/list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/conversion_eqs?lookback_period=1d' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/conversion_eqs`

Get the Event Quality Score (EQS) of your conversion signals.

[Event Quality Score](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/eqs) indicates how effective the customer information and event insights (metadata) passed with your web, app and offline conversion events may be at matching to a Pinterest user.

<h3 id="get-event-quality-score-eqs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lookback_period|query|[LookbackPeriodOptions](#schemalookbackperiodoptions)|true|Lookback window (number of days).|
|source_platform|query|[SourcePlatformOptions](#schemasourceplatformoptions)|false|Source platform of event.|
|ingestion_source|query|[IngestionSourceOptions](#schemaingestionsourceoptions)|false|Ingestion source of event.|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|lookback_period|1d|
|lookback_period|14d|
|source_platform|WEB|
|source_platform|MOBILE|
|source_platform|MOBILE_ANDROID|
|source_platform|MOBILE_IOS|
|source_platform|OFFLINE|
|source_platform|PINTEREST_WEB|
|source_platform|PINTEREST_ANDROID|
|source_platform|PINTEREST_IOS|
|source_platform|POINT_OF_SALE|
|ingestion_source|TAG|
|ingestion_source|MMP|
|ingestion_source|FILE_UPLOAD|
|ingestion_source|CONVERSIONS_API|
|ingestion_source|NATIVE|

<h1 id="pinterest-rest-api-conversionevents">conversion_events</h1>

Submit conversion events via the Pinterest API.

## Send conversions

<a id="opIdevents/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/events \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
```

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/events`

The Pinterest API offers advertisers a way to send Pinterest their conversion information (including web conversions, in-app conversions, or even offline conversions) based on their `ad_account_id`. The request body should be a JSON object.
- This endpoint requires an `access_token` be generated through Ads Manager. Review the [Conversions Guide](/docs/api-features/conversion-overview/) for more details. (Note that the authorization header required is `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`).
- The token's `user_account` must either be the Owner of the specified ad account, or have one of the necessary roles granted to them via [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts): Admin, Analyst, Audience, Campaign. (Note that the token can be used across multiple ad accounts under an user ID.)
- This endpoint has a rate limit of 5,000 calls per minute per ad account.
- If the merchant is submitting this information using both Pinterest conversion tags and the Pinterest API, Pinterest will remove duplicate information before reporting. (Note that events that took place offline cannot be deduplicated.)

Use this mode to verify your requests are working and your events are constructed correctly.<br>Warning: If you use this query parameter, be certain that it is off (set to false or deleted) before sending a legitimate (non-testing) request.|
|body|body|[ConversionEventsCreate](#schemaconversioneventscreate)|true|none|
|» data|body|[[ConversionEventsDataItems](#schemaconversioneventsdataitems)]|true|A list of events (one or more) encapsulated by a data object.|

<h1 id="pinterest-rest-api-conversiontags">conversion_tags</h1>
