## Create conversion tag

<a id="opIdconversion_tags/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/conversion_tags \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "aem_db_enabled": false,
    "aem_enabled": false,
    "aem_external_id_enabled": false,
    "aem_fnln_enabled": false,
    "aem_ge_enabled": false,
    "aem_loc_enabled": false,
    "aem_ph_enabled": false,
    "md_frequency": 0.6,
    "name": "download_picture"
  }'
```

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/conversion_tags`

Create a conversion tag, also known as [Pinterest tag](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/set-up-the-pinterest-tag), with the option to enable enhanced match.

The Pinterest Tag tracks actions people take on the ad account's website after they view the ad account's ad on Pinterest. The advertiser needs to customize this tag to track conversions.

For more information, see:

[Set up the Pinterest tag](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/set-up-the-pinterest-tag)

[Pinterest Tag](/docs/track-conversions/pinterest-tag/)

[Enhanced match](/docs/track-conversions/pinterest-tag/#enhanced-match)

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "aem_db_enabled": false,
  "aem_enabled": false,
  "aem_external_id_enabled": false,
  "aem_fnln_enabled": false,
  "aem_ge_enabled": false,
  "aem_loc_enabled": false,
  "aem_ph_enabled": false,
  "md_frequency": 0.6,
  "name": "download_picture"
}
```

<h3 id="create-conversion-tag-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|body|body|[ConversionTagCreate](#schemaconversiontagcreate)|true|none|
|» aem_db_enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether Automatic Enhanced Match birthdate is enabled. See [Enhanced match](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/enhanced-match) for more information.|
|» aem_enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether Automatic Enhanced Match email is enabled. See [Enhanced match](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/enhanced-match) for more information.|
|» aem_external_id_enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether Automatic Enhanced Match location is enabled. See [Enhanced match](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/enhanced-match) for more information.|
|» aem_fnln_enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether Automatic Enhanced Match name is enabled. See [Enhanced match](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/enhanced-match) for more information.|
|» aem_ge_enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether Automatic Enhanced Match gender is enabled. See [Enhanced match](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/enhanced-match) for more information.|
|» aem_loc_enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether Automatic Enhanced Match location is enabled. See [Enhanced match](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/enhanced-match) for more information.|
|» aem_ph_enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether Automatic Enhanced Match phone is enabled. See [Enhanced match](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/enhanced-match) for more information.|
|» md_frequency|body|number \| null|false|Metadata ingestion frequency.|
|» name|body|string|true|Conversion tag name.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

  "code_snippet": "<script type=text/javascript> [...]",
  "configs": {
    "aem_db_enabled": false,
    "aem_enabled": false,
    "aem_external_id_enabled": false,
    "aem_fnln_enabled": false,
    "aem_ge_enabled": false,
    "aem_loc_enabled": false,
    "aem_ph_enabled": false,
    "md_frequency": 0.6,
    "no_code_capi_domains": [
      "https://sub.exampledomain.com"
    ]
  },
  "enhanced_match_status": "VALIDATION_COMPLETE",
  "id": "2617998078212",

<h1 id="pinterest-rest-api-customerlistuploads">customer_list_uploads</h1>

View, create, or manage customer list uploads.

## Create customer list upload

<a id="opIdcustomer_list_uploads/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/customer_lists/string/uploads \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "operation": "REMOVE",
    "total_parts": 2
  }'
```

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/customer_lists/{customer_list_id}/uploads`

Create a customer list upload request for multipart S3 upload.

Note: Each part must be at least 5mb; however the last part can be any size greater than 0.
Clients with smaller files can request a single part count. This minimal part size restriction is defined by the AWS S3 API.

**Please review the [update customer list endpoint](/docs/api/v5/customer_lists-update/) documentation for additional information.**

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "operation": "REMOVE",
  "total_parts": 2
}
```

<h3 id="create-customer-list-upload-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|none|
|customer_list_id|path|string|true|Customer list ID.|
|body|body|[CustomerListUploadCreateRequest](#schemacustomerlistuploadcreaterequest)|true|none|
|» operation|body|[UserListOperationType](#schemauserlistoperationtype)|true|User list operation type (add or remove)|
|» total_parts|body|integer|true|Number of parts to upload the file in.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|

|» operation|REMOVE|

<h1 id="pinterest-rest-api-customerlists">customer_lists</h1>

View, create, or update customer lists.

## Get customer lists

<a id="opIdcustomer_lists/list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/customer_lists \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/customer_lists`

Get a set of customer lists including id and name based on the filters provided.

(Customer lists are a type of audience.) For more information, see [Audience targeting](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/audience-targeting) or the [Audiences](/docs/api-features/targeting-overview/) section of the ads management guide.

<h3 id="get-customer-lists-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|none|
|bookmark|query|string|false|Cursor used to fetch the next page of items|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Maximum number of items to include in a single page.<br>See documentation on [Pagination](/docs/reference/pagination/) for more information.|
|order|query|[Pinterest.Lib.PaginationOrder](#schemapinterest.lib.paginationorder)|false|The order in which to sort the items returned: "ASCENDING" or "DESCENDING" by ID.<br>Note that higher-value IDs are associated with more-recently added items.|
|exclude_nca|query|boolean|false|When true, excludes customer lists uploaded for new customer acquisition (expanded matching) from the result. Defaults to false (include all).|

#### Enumerated Values

## Create customer lists

<a id="opIdcustomer_lists/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/customer_lists \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "is_nca": true,
    "list_type": "EMAIL",
    "name": "The Glengarry Glen Ross leads",
    "records": "email1@pinterest.com,email2@pinterest.com,..<more records>",
    "records_v2": [
      {
        "email": "string",
        "external_id": "string",
        "hashed_phone_number": "string",
        "hashed_pinner_id": "string",
        "ip_address": "string",
        "liveramp_envelope": "string",
        "maid": "string",
        "user_agent": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/customer_lists`

Create a customer list from your records (hashed or plain-text email addresses, or hashed MAIDs or IDFAs).

A customer list is one of the four types of Pinterest audiences: for more information, see [Audience targeting](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/audience-targeting) or the [Audiences](/docs/api-features/targeting-overview/) section of the ads management guide.

**Please review our [requirements](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/audience-targeting#section-13341) for what type of information is allowed when uploading a customer list.**
 
When you create a customer list, the system scans the list for existing Pinterest accounts; the list must include at least 100 Pinterest accounts. Your original list will be deleted when the matching process is complete. The filtered list – containing only the Pinterest accounts that were included in your starting list – is what will be used to create the audience.
 
To use your customer list after creating it, convert it into a customer list audience by passing the `CUSTOMER_LIST` audience type at the [create audience endpoint](https://developer.pinterest.com/docs/api/v5/audiences-create).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "is_nca": true,
  "list_type": "EMAIL",
  "name": "The Glengarry Glen Ross leads",
  "records": "email1@pinterest.com,email2@pinterest.com,..<more records>",
  "records_v2": [
    {
      "email": "string",
      "external_id": "string",
      "hashed_phone_number": "string",
      "hashed_pinner_id": "string",
      "ip_address": "string",
      "liveramp_envelope": "string",
      "maid": "string",
      "user_agent": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-customer-lists-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[CustomerListCreate](#schemacustomerlistcreate)|true|none|
|» is_nca|body|boolean|false|Whether the list was uploaded for new customer acquisition (expanded matching). Immutable after creation.|
|» list_type|body|object|false|Type of customer list (e.g., EMAIL, IDFA, MAID).|
|» name|body|string|true|Customer list name.|
|» records|body|string|false|Records list. Can be any combination of emails, MAIDs, or IDFAs. Emails must be lowercase and can be plain text or hashed using SHA1, SHA256, or MD5. MAIDs and IDFAs must be hashed with SHA1, SHA256, or MD5.|
|» records_v2|body|[[CustomerListRecordRow](#schemacustomerlistrecordrow)]|false|Multi-field record format. Array of objects with optional email, maid, ip_address, user_agent, external_id, hashed_pinner_id, hashed_phone_number, and liveramp_envelope per row. Provide exactly one of records or records_v2.|

`PATCH /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/customer_lists/{customer_list_id}`

Append or remove records to/from an existing customer list. (A customer list is one of the four types of Pinterest audiences.)

When you add records to an existing customer list, the system scans the additions for existing Pinterest accounts; those are the records that will be added to your "CUSTOMER_LIST" audience. Your original list of records to add will be deleted when the matching process is complete.

For more information, see [Audience targeting](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/audience-targeting) or the [Audiences](/docs/api-features/targeting-overview/) section of the ads management guide.

> Body parameter

```json

  "operation_type": {},
  "records": "email1@pinterest.com,email2@pinterest.com,..<more records>",
  "records_v2": [
    {
      "email": "string",
      "external_id": "string",
      "hashed_phone_number": "string",
      "hashed_pinner_id": "string",
      "ip_address": "string",
      "liveramp_envelope": "string",
      "maid": "string",

    }

}

|» records_v2|body|[[CustomerListRecordRow](#schemacustomerlistrecordrow)]|false|Multi-field record format. Array of objects with optional email, maid, ip_address, user_agent, external_id, hashed_pinner_id, hashed_phone_number, and liveramp_envelope per row. Provide exactly one of records or records_v2.|

<h1 id="pinterest-rest-api-keywords">keywords</h1>

View, create or update keywords.

## Get keywords

<a id="opIdkeywords/get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/keywords \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/keywords`

    Get a list of keywords based on the filters provided. If no filter is provided, it will default to the `ad_account_id` filter, which means it will only return keywords that specifically have `parent_id` set to the `ad_account_id`. Note: Keywords can have `ad_account_ids`, `campaign_ids`, and `ad_group_ids` set as their `parent_ids`. Keywords created through Ads Manager will have their `parent_id` set to an `ad_group_id`, not `ad_account_id`.

    For more information, see [Keyword targeting](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/keyword-targeting).

    **Notes:**
    - Advertisers and campaigns can only be assigned keywords with excluding (`_NEGATIVE`).
    - All keyword match types are available for ad groups.

    For more information on match types, see [match type enums](/docs/api-features/targeting-overview/).

    **Returns:**
    - A successful call returns an object containing an array of new keyword objects and an empty `errors` object array.
    - An unsuccessful call returns an empty keywords array, and instead, inserts the entire object with nulled/negated properties into the `errors` object array:
      ```json
      {
        "keywords": [],
        "errors": [
          {
            "data": {
              "archived": null,
              "match_type": "EXACT",
              "parent_type": null,
              "value": "foobar",
              "parent_id": null,
              "type": "keyword",
              "id": null
            },
            "error_messages": [
              "Advertisers and Campaigns only accept excluded targeting attributes."
            ]
          }
        ]
      }

<h3 id="get-keywords-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|campaign_id|query|string|false|Campaign Id to use to filter the results.|
|ad_group_id|query|string|false|Ad group Id.|
|ad_group_ids|query|[[Pinterest.Lib.IntegerFormatType](#schemapinterest.lib.integerformattype)]|false|List of Ad group Ids to retrieve keywords from. This feature is currently in BETA and is not available to all users.|
|match_types|query|[[MatchType](#schemamatchtype)]|false|Keyword [match type](/docs/api-features/targeting-overview/)|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|bookmark|query|string|false|Cursor used to fetch the next page of items|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Maximum number of items to include in a single page.<br>See documentation on [Pagination](/docs/reference/pagination/) for more information.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|match_types|BROAD|
|match_types|PHRASE|
|match_types|EXACT|
|match_types|EXACT_NEGATIVE|
|match_types|PHRASE_NEGATIVE|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "bookmark": "string",
  "items": [
    {
      "archived": false,
      "bid": 0,
      "id": "383791336903426391",
      "match_type": {},
      "parent_id": "383791336903426391",
      "parent_type": "campaign",
      "type": "keyword",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

}
```

}

## Create keywords

<a id="opIdkeywords/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/keywords \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "keywords": [
      {
        "bid": 0,
        "match_type": {},
        "value": "string"
      }
    ],
    "parent_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/keywords`

  Create keywords for the following entity types (advertiser, campaign, ad group, or ad). For more information, see [Keyword targeting](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/keyword-targeting).

  **Notes:**
  - Advertisers and campaigns can only be assigned keywords with excluding (`_NEGATIVE`).
  - All keyword match types are available for ad groups.

  For more information on match types, see [match type enums](/docs/api-features/targeting-overview/).

  **Returns:**
  - A successful call returns an object containing an array of new keyword objects and an empty `errors` object array.
  - An unsuccessful call returns an empty keywords array, and instead, inserts the entire object with nulled/negated properties into the `errors` object array:
    ```json
    {
      "keywords": [],
      "errors": [
        {
          "data": {
            "archived": null,
            "match_type": "EXACT",
            "parent_type": null,
            "value": "foobar",
            "parent_id": null,
            "type": "keyword",
            "id": null
          },
          "error_messages": [
            "Advertisers and Campaigns only accept excluded targeting attributes."
          ]
        }
      ]
    }

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "keywords": [
    {
      "bid": 0,
      "match_type": {},
      "value": "string"
    }
  ],
  "parent_id": "string"
}
```

## Update keywords

<a id="opIdkeywords/update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/keywords \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \

      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/keywords`

  Update one or more keywords' bid and archived fields. Archiving
  a keyword effectively deletes it - keywords no longer receive metrics and
  are no longer visible within the parent entity's keywords list.

> Body parameter

```json

  "keywords": [

      "archived": false,
      "bid": 0,
      "id": "383791336903426391"

}

## List trending keywords

<a id="opIdtrending_keywords/list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/trends/keywords/GB%2BIE/top/monthly \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /trends/keywords/{region}/top/{trend_type}`

Get the top trending search keywords among the Pinterest user audience.

Trending keywords can be used to inform ad targeting, budget strategy, and creative decisions about which products and Pins will resonate with your audience.

Geographic, demographic and interest-based filters are available to narrow down to the top trends among a specific audience. Multiple trend types are supported that can be used to identify newly-popular, evergreen or seasonal keywords.

For an interactive way to explore this data, please visit [trends.pinterest.com](https://trends.pinterest.com).

<h3 id="list-trending-keywords-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|region|path|[TrendsSupportedRegion](#schematrendssupportedregion)|true|  The geographic region of interest. Only top trends within the specified region will be returned.<br><br>  The `region` parameter is formatted as ISO 3166-2 country codes delimited by `+`, corresponding to the following geographic areas:<br>  - `US` - United States<br>  - `CA` - Canada<br>  - `DE` - Germany<br>  - `FR` - France<br>  - `ES` - Spain<br>  - `IT` - Italy<br>  - `DE+AT+CH` - Germanic countries<br>  - `GB+IE` - Great Britain & Ireland<br>  - `IT+ES+PT+GR+MT` - Southern Europe<br>  - `PL+RO+HU+SK+CZ` - Eastern Europe<br>  - `SE+DK+FI+NO` - Nordic countries<br>  - `NL+BE+LU` - Benelux<br>  - `AR` - Argentina<br>  - `BR` - Brazil<br>  - `CO` - Colombia<br>  - `MX` - Mexico<br>  - `MX+AR+CO+CL` - Hispanic LatAm<br>  - `AU+NZ` - Australasia|
|trend_type|path|[TrendType](#schematrendtype)|true|  The methodology used to rank how trendy a keyword is.<br>  - `growing` trends have high upward growth in search volume over the last quarter<br>  - `monthly` trends have high search volume in the last month<br>  - `yearly` trends have high search volume in the last year<br>  - `seasonal` trends have high upward growth in search volume over the last month and exhibit a seasonal recurring pattern (typically annual)|
|interests|query|[[TrendsL1Interest](#schematrendsl1interest)]|false|  The list of supported interests is:<br>  - `animals` - Animals<br>  - `architecture` - Architecture<br>  - `art` - Art<br>  - `beauty` - Beauty<br>  - `childrens_fashion` - Children's Fashion<br>  - `design` - Design<br>  - `diy_and_crafts` - DIY & Crafts<br>  - `education` - Education<br>  - `electronics` - Electronics<br>  - `entertainment` - Entertainment<br>  - `event_planning` - Event Planning<br>  - `finance` - Finance<br>  - `food_and_drinks` - Food & Drink<br>  - `gardening` - Gardening<br>  - `health` - Health<br>  - `home_decor` - Home Decor<br>  - `mens_fashion` - Men's Fashion<br>  - `parenting` - Parenting<br>  - `quotes` - Quotes<br>  - `sport` - Sports<br>  - `travel` - Travel<br>  - `vehicles` - Vehicles<br>  - `wedding` - Wedding<br>  - `womens_fashion` - Women's Fashion|
|genders|query|[[TrendsGenderFilter](#schematrendsgenderfilter)]|false|If set, filters the results to trends among users who identify with the<br>specified gender(s). If unset, trends among all genders will be returned.<br>The `unknown` group includes users with unspecified or customized gender<br>profile settings.|
|ages|query|[[TrendsAgeBucket](#schematrendsagebucket)]|false|If set, filters the results to trends among users in the specified age<br>range(s). If unset, trends among all age groups will be returned.|
|include_keywords|query|[KeywordList](#schemakeywordlist)|false|If set, filters the results to top trends which include at least one of<br>the specified keywords. If unset, no keyword filtering logic is applied.|
|normalize_against_group|query|boolean|false| Governs how the resulting time series data will be normalized to a [0-100] scale.<br><br>  By default (`false`), the data will be normalized independently for each keyword.  The peak search volume observation in *each* keyword's time series will be represented by the value 100.  This is ideal for analyzing when an individual keyword is expected to peak in interest.<br><br>  If set to `true`, the data will be normalized as a group.  The peak search volume observation across *all* keywords in the response will be represented by the value 100, and all other values scaled accordingly.  Use this option when you wish to compare relative search volume between multiple keywords.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The maximum number of trending keywords that will be returned. Keywords<br>are returned in trend-ranked order, so a `limit` of 50 will return the<br>top 50 trends.|
|include_demographics|query|boolean|false|Including the age and gender distribution for each keyword. By default<br>(`false`), the response will not include demographics data.|

## Create lead ads subscription

<a id="opIdad_accounts_subscriptions/post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/leads/subscriptions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "lead_form_id": "string",
    "webhook_url": "string",
    "partner_access_token": "string",
    "partner_metadata": {
      "subscriber_key": "string"
    },
    "partner_refresh_token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/leads/subscriptions`

Create a lead ads webhook subscription.
Subscriptions allow Pinterest to deliver lead data from Ads Manager directly to the subscriber. Subscriptions can exist for a specific lead form or at ad account level.
  - Only requests for the OWNER or ADMIN of the ad_account will be allowed.
  - Advertisers can set up multiple integrations using ad_account_id + lead_form_id but only one integration per unique records.
  - For data security, egress lead data is encrypted with AES-256-GCM.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "lead_form_id": "string",
  "webhook_url": "string",
  "partner_access_token": "string",
  "partner_metadata": {
    "subscriber_key": "string"
  },
  "partner_refresh_token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-lead-ads-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|body|body|[LeadSubscriptionPostParamsCreate](#schemaleadsubscriptionpostparamscreate)|true|none|
|» lead_form_id|body|string|false|Lead form ID.|
|» webhook_url|body|string|true|Standard HTTPS webhook URL.|
|» partner_access_token|body|string|false|Partner access token. Only for clients that requires authentication. We recommend to avoid this param.|
|» partner_metadata|body|object|false|Partner metadata. Only for clients that requires special handling. We recommend to avoid this param.|
|» » subscriber_key|body|string|false|Text field value that uniquely identifies a subscriber.|
|» partner_refresh_token|body|string|false|Partner refresh token. Only for clients that requires authentication. We recommend to avoid this param.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "ad_account_id": "string",
  "api_version": "string",
  "created_time": 0,
  "cryptographic_algorithm": "string",
  "cryptographic_key": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "lead_form_id": "string",
  "user_account_id": "string",
  "webhook_url": "string"
}
```

  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}

## Create a request to export leads collected from a lead ad

<a id="opIdleads_export/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/leads_export \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{

  }'
```

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/leads_export`

**This feature is currently in beta and not available to all apps. If you're interested in joining the beta, please reach out to your Pinterest account manager.**

Create an export of leads collected from a lead ad. This returns a `leads_export_id` token that you can use to download the export when it is ready.

Note: Lead ad data will be available up to 30 days after the lead has been submitted.

For more, see [Lead ads](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/lead-ads).

```json
{
  "ad_id": "687201361754",
  "end_date": "2020-12-20",
  "start_date": "2020-12-20"

## Register media upload

<a id="opIdmedia/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/media \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "media_type": "video"
  }'
```

`POST /media`

Register your intent to upload media.

The response includes all of the information needed to upload the media to Pinterest.

To upload the media, make an HTTP POST request (using `curl`, for example) to `upload_url` using the `Content-Type` header value. Send the media file's contents as the request's `file` parameter and also include all of the parameters from `upload_parameters`.

**[Learn more](/docs/api-features/creating-boards-and-pins/#creating-video-pins)** about video Pin creation.

> Body parameter

{
  "media_type": "video"
}

<h1 id="pinterest-rest-api-msotevents">msot_events</h1>

Submit Measurement Source of Truth attributed conversion events via the Pinterest API.

## Send Measurement Source Of Truth (MSOT) attributed conversion events

<a id="opIdmsot_events/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/msot/events \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "action_timestamps": [
      1451410040
    ],
    "ad_group_id": "2680060704746",
    "attribution_model": "multi_touch",
    "attribution_scope": "click",
    "attribution_score": 0.5,
    "campaign_id": "626736533506",
    "click_window": "string",
    "currency": {},
    "event_id": "eventId0001",
    "event_name": "add_to_cart",
    "event_timestamp": 1451431341,
    "total_event_touchpoints": 2,
    "total_events": 2,
    "total_events_fractional": 0.1,
    "value": 123.45,
    "view_window": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/msot/events`

**This feature is currently in beta and not available to all apps.**
If you are interested in joining the beta, reach out to your Pinterest account manager.

Advertisers or their measurement partners can send attributed MSOT conversion events to Pinterest
based on their `ad_account_id`. The request body should be a JSON object.

- These events will not be used in Reporting.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "action_timestamps": [
    1451410040
  ],
  "ad_group_id": "2680060704746",
  "attribution_model": "multi_touch",
  "attribution_scope": "click",
  "attribution_score": 0.5,
  "campaign_id": "626736533506",
  "click_window": "string",
  "currency": {},
  "event_id": "eventId0001",
  "event_name": "add_to_cart",
  "event_timestamp": 1451431341,
  "total_event_touchpoints": 2,
  "total_events": 2,
  "total_events_fractional": 0.1,
  "value": 123.45,
  "view_window": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="send-measurement-source-of-truth-msot-attributed-conversion-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|body|body|[ConversionMSOTEventsCreate](#schemaconversionmsoteventscreate)|true|none|
|» action_timestamps|body|[integer(int64)]|false|Timestamp(s) when the ad action(s) happened. Unix timestamp in seconds.|
|» ad_group_id|body|object|true|The ID of the ad group that was attributed to the conversion event.|
|» attribution_model|body|object|false|The attribution model used to attribute the conversion event.|
|» attribution_scope|body|object|false|Ad event type.|
|» attribution_score|body|number(double)|false|Credit given to the attributed ad actions. Allowed values are > 0 and <= 1.|
|» campaign_id|body|object|false|The ID of the campaign that was attributed to the conversion event.|
|» click_window|body|string|false|Click window used for attribution (for example, `1d`, `7d`, `30d`, `lifetime`).|
|» currency|body|object|false|Currency code for the `value` field, required if `value` is present. Currency Codes should be in ISO 4217 standard.|
|» event_id|body|string|true|A unique id string that identifies this event. If you are already sending us events through Conversions API,<br>then this id should match the event_id sent through Conversions API.|
|» event_name|body|object|true|Type of user event.|
|» event_timestamp|body|integer(int64)|true|The time when the event occurred. Unix timestamp in seconds.|
|» total_event_touchpoints|body|integer|false|Total number of ad events including other non-Pinterest ad platforms.|
|» total_events|body|integer|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: use `total_events_fractional` instead to avoid rounding errors.<br>Total number of conversion events that are reported in one API call.<br><br>If you are sending one API request for one attributed conversion event then this value should be 1.<br>If you are sending multiple attributed conversion events in one API request then this value should be<br>the total number of attributed conversion events in the request.|
|» total_events_fractional|body|number(double)|false|Total number of conversion events that are reported in one API call. Use this field instead of<br>`total_events` to send precise fractional values.<br><br>If you are sending one API request for one attributed conversion event with full credit, this value should be 1.0.<br>For partial attribution, send the exact fractional value (e.g., 0.5 for half credit).|
|» value|body|number(double)|false|Order value of the conversion event. Required if `event_name` is `add_to_cart` or `checkout`.|
|» view_window|body|string|false|View window used for attribution (for example, `1d`, `7d`, `30d`).|

> Example responses

{}
```

  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

> 401 Response

  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

```json
{
  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

```json
{
  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

## Generate OAuth access token

<a id="opIdoauth/token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/oauth/token \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'code=string&continuous_refresh=string&grant_type=authorization_code&redirect_uri=string&refresh_token=string&scope=string'
```

`POST /oauth/token`

Generate a new OAuth access token using an authorization code; or refresh an existing one using a continuous refresh token.

Follow the complete steps for [requesting and refreshing tokens](/docs/getting-started/set-up-authentication-and-authorization/).

**Note:** If your app was created **before September 25, 2025**, make sure to set the `continuous_refresh` parameter to `true` to use the continuous refresh token (60-day expiration, refreshable indefinitely). Pinterest no longer supports the legacy refresh token (365-day expiration, hard limit).

Disregard this note if your app was activated on or after September 25, 2025. You are automatically using the continuous refresh token.

Use [Token Debugger](/docs/developer-tools/token-debugger/) to validate and inspect your access token.


> Body parameter

```yaml
code: string
continuous_refresh: string
grant_type: authorization_code
redirect_uri: string
refresh_token: string
scope: string
```

<h3 id="generate-oauth-access-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[OauthAccessTokenCreate](#schemaoauthaccesstokencreate)|true|none|
|» code|body|string|false|none|
|» continuous_refresh|body|string|false|  If your app was created before **September 25, 2025**, set to `true` to generate a [continuous refresh token](/docs/getting-started/set-up-authentication-and-authorization/#exchange-the-default-refresh-token-for-a-continuous-refresh-token), which has a 60-day expiration window. We no longer support the legacy refresh token, which has a 365-day expiration window.<br><br>  If your app was created on or after **September 25, 2025**, ignore this parameter. You automatically receive a continuous refresh token when you request an access token.|
|» grant_type|body|[TokenGrantType](#schematokengranttype)|true|The type of OAuth grant being requested.|
|» redirect_uri|body|string|false|none|
|» refresh_token|body|string|false|none|
|» scope|body|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» grant_type|authorization_code|
|» grant_type|refresh_token|
|» grant_type|client_credentials|

  "refresh_token_expires_in": 0,

}
```

## Revoke a token

<a id="opIdtoken/revoke"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/oauth/token/revoke \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'token=pinr.eyJhbGciOiJS...&token_type_hint=%7B%7D'
```

`POST /oauth/token/revoke`

Revokes an access or refresh token. Only tokens issued for system users are currently supported. Revoked tokens become immediately invalid and unusable.

> Body parameter

```yaml
token: pinr.eyJhbGciOiJS...
token_type_hint: {}
```

<h3 id="revoke-a-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TokenRevocationRequestCreate](#schematokenrevocationrequestcreate)|true|none|
|» token|body|string|true|The token to revoke.|
|» token_type_hint|body|object|false|The type of the token to revoke. Please refer to [our developer guide for more information](https://developers.pinterest.com/docs/getting-started/set-up-authentication-and-authorization/) for more information.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

<h1 id="pinterest-rest-api-pins">pins</h1>

View, create, update, or delete information about Pins.

## List Pins

<a id="opIdpins/list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/pins \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /pins`

    Get a list of the Pins owned by the "operation user_account".
    - By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.
    - All Pins owned by the "operation user_account" are included, regardless of who owns the board they are on.

    Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account".

    Disclaimer: There are known performance issues when filtering by field `creative_type` and including protected pins.
    If your request is timing out in this scenario, we encourage you to use [GET List Pins on Board](/docs/api/v5/#operation/boards/list_pins).

<h3 id="list-pins-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pin_filter|query|[PinFilter](#schemapinfilter)|false|The filter to apply to the pins|
|pin_metrics|query|boolean|false|Specify whether to return 90d and lifetime Pin metrics. Total comments<br>and total reactions are only available with lifetime Pin metrics. If Pin was<br>created before `2023-03-20` lifetime metrics will only be available<br>for Video and Idea Pin formats. Lifetime metrics are available for all Pin<br>formats since then.|
|include_protected_pins|query|boolean|false|Whether to include protected pins in the results|
|pin_type|query|[PinType](#schemapintype)|false|The type of pins to return, currently only enabled for private pins|
|creative_types|query|[[CreativeType](#schemacreativetype)]|false|Pin creative types filter. **Note:** SHOP_THE_PIN has been deprecated. Please use COLLECTION instead.|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|domain|query|string|false|Only return pins with links that match the exact domain. Domain should not include 'www.' prefix. For example, 'pinterest.com' is a valid domain, but 'www.pinterest.com' is not (will not match any pins).|
|domains|query|[string]|false|Only return pins with links whose domain matches any value in the list.<br>Values are joined comma-separated on the wire<br>(e.g. `?domains=instagram.com,jcpenney.com`).|
|include_product_tag_obj|query|boolean|false|Include product tag objects in the response with their associated links.|
|bookmark|query|string|false|Cursor used to fetch the next page of items|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Maximum number of items to include in a single page.<br>See documentation on [Pagination](/docs/reference/pagination/) for more information.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|pin_filter|exclude_native|
|pin_filter|exclude_repins|
|pin_filter|has_been_promoted|
|pin_type|PRIVATE|
|creative_types|REGULAR|
|creative_types|VIDEO|
|creative_types|SHOPPING|
|creative_types|CAROUSEL|
|creative_types|MAX_VIDEO|
|creative_types|SHOP_THE_PIN|
|creative_types|COLLECTION|
|creative_types|IDEA|
|creative_types|SHOWCASE|
|creative_types|QUIZ|
|creative_types|COLLAGE|
|creative_types|MAX_WIDTH_REGULAR_COLLECTION|
|creative_types|MAX_WIDTH_VIDEO_COLLECTION|
|creative_types|APP|

## Create Pin

<a id="opIdpins/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/pins \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ai_disclosures": {
      "values": [
        "AI_MODIFIED"
      ]
    },
    "alt_text": "string",
    "board_id": "string",
    "board_section_id": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "dominant_color": "string",
    "link": "string",
    "media_source": {
      "content_type": "image/jpeg",
      "data": "string",
      "is_standard": true,
      "source_type": "image_base64"
    },
    "parent_pin_id": "string",
    "sponsor_id": "string",
    "title": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /pins`

 Create a Pin on a board or board section owned by the "operation user_account".

 Note: If the current "operation user_account" (defined by the access token) has access to another user's Ad Accounts via Pinterest Business Access, you can modify your request to make use of the current operation_user_account's permissions to those Ad Accounts by including the ad_account_id in the path parameters for the request (e.g. .../?ad_account_id=12345&...).

- This function is intended solely for publishing new content created by the user. If you are interested in saving content created by others to your Pinterest boards, sometimes called 'curated content', please use our [Save button](/docs/web-features/add-ons-overview/) instead. For more tips on creating fresh content for Pinterest, review our [Content App Solutions Guide](/docs/api-features/content-overview/).

**[Learn more](/docs/api-features/creating-boards-and-pins/#creating-video-pins)** about video Pin creation.

**[Learn more](/docs/api-features/creating-boards-and-pins/#creating-image-pins)** about image Pin creation.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ai_disclosures": {
    "values": [
      "AI_MODIFIED"
    ]
  },
  "alt_text": "string",
  "board_id": "string",
  "board_section_id": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "dominant_color": "string",
  "link": "string",
  "media_source": {
    "content_type": "image/jpeg",
    "data": "string",
    "is_standard": true,
    "source_type": "image_base64"
  },
  "parent_pin_id": "string",
  "sponsor_id": "string",
  "title": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-pin-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|body|body|[PinCreate](#schemapincreate)|true|none|
|» ai_disclosures|body|object|false|AI disclosure declarations the creator has made about this Pin.|
|» » values|body|[[AiDisclosureItem](#schemaaidisclosureitem)]|true|List of AI disclosure declarations the creator has made about this Pin.|
|» alt_text|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» board_id|body|string|false|The board to which this Pin belongs.|
|» board_section_id|body|string \| null|false|The board section to which this Pin belongs.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» dominant_color|body|string \| null|false|Dominant pin color. Hex number, e.g. `#6E7874`.|
|» link|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» media_source|body|[PinMediaSource](#schemapinmediasource)|false|Pin media source that can be an image, video, or a mix of both passed in as a request.|
|» parent_pin_id|body|string \| null|false|The source pin id if this pin was saved from another pin. [Learn more](https://help.pinterest.com/article/save-pins-on-pinterest).|
|» sponsor_id|body|string \| null|false|The sponsor account id to request paid partnership from.  Currently the field is only available to a list of users in a closed beta.|
|» title|body|string \| null|false|none|

## Get multiple Pin analytics

<a id="opIdmulti_pins/analytics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/pins/analytics?pin_ids=string&start_date=1970-01-01&end_date=1970-01-01&metric_types=IMPRESSION' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /pins/analytics`

**This endpoint is currently in beta and not available to all apps. [Learn more](/docs/getting-started/using-beta-and-restricted-features/).**

Get analytics for multiple pins owned by the "operation user_account" - or on a group board that has been shared with this account.
- The maximum number of pins supported in a single request is 100.
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account:

- For Pins on public or protected boards: Admin, Analyst.
- For Pins on secret boards: Admin.

If Pin was created before `2023-03-20` lifetime metrics will only be available for Video and Idea Pin formats. Lifetime metrics are available for all Pin formats since then.

<h3 id="get-multiple-pin-analytics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pin_ids|query|[[Pinterest.Lib.IntegerFormatType](#schemapinterest.lib.integerformattype)]|true|List of Pin IDs.|
|start_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report start date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days back from today.|
|end_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report end date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days past start_date.|
|app_types|query|string|false|Apps or devices to get data for, default is all.|
|metric_types|query|[[MultiPinsAnalyticsMetricTypesItem](#schemamultipinsanalyticsmetrictypesitem)]|true|Pin metric types to get data for.|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

|app_types|MOBILE|
|app_types|TABLET|
|app_types|WEB|
|metric_types|IMPRESSION|

|metric_types|PIN_CLICK|
|metric_types|SAVE|
|metric_types|SAVE_RATE|
|metric_types|TOTAL_COMMENTS|

`GET /pins/{pin_id}`

  Get a Pin owned by the "operation user_account" - or on a group board that has been shared with this account.

  Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account:

        "title": "string"

    "description": "string",
    "link": "string",
    "title": "string"
  }'

`PATCH /pins/{pin_id}`

Update a pin owned by the "operating user_account".
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". - For Pins on public or protected boards: Owner, Admin, Analyst, Campaign Manager.

## Get Pin analytics

<a id="opIdpins/analytics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/pins/string/analytics?start_date=1970-01-01&end_date=1970-01-01&metric_types=IMPRESSION' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /pins/{pin_id}/analytics`

Get analytics for a Pin owned by the "operation user_account" - or on a group board that has been shared with this account.
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account:

- For Pins on public or protected boards: Admin, Analyst.
- For Pins on secret boards: Admin.

If Pin was created before `2023-03-20` lifetime metrics will only be available for Video and Idea Pin formats. Lifetime metrics are available for all Pin formats since then.

<h3 id="get-pin-analytics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pin_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of a Pin.|
|start_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report start date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days back from today.|
|end_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report end date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days past start_date.|
|app_types|query|string|false|Apps or devices to get data for, default is all.|
|metric_types|query|[[QuerypinanalyticsmetrictypesItems](#schemaquerypinanalyticsmetrictypesitems)]|true|Pin metric types to get data for. VIDEO_MRC_VIEW are Video views, VIDEO_V50_WATCH_TIME is Total play time. If Pin was created before `2023-03-20`, Profile visits and Follows will only be available for Idea Pins. These metrics are available for all Pin formats since then. Keep in mind this cannot have ALL if split_field is set to any value other than `NO_SPLIT`.|
|split_field|query|string|false|How to split the data into groups. Not including this param means data won't be split.|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|app_types|ALL|
|app_types|MOBILE|
|app_types|TABLET|
|app_types|WEB|
|split_field|NO_SPLIT|
|split_field|APP_TYPE|

## Save Pin

<a id="opIdpins/save"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/pins/string/save \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "board_id": "string",
    "board_section_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /pins/{pin_id}/save`

Save a Pin on a board or board section owned by the "operation user_account".
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.
Optional: Business Access: Specify an `ad_account_id` (obtained via [List ad accounts](/docs/api/v5/#operation/ad_accounts/list)) to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". In order to do this, the token user_account must have one of the following [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts) roles on the ad_account:

- For Pins on public or protected boards: Owner, Admin, Analyst, Campaign Manager.
- For Pins on secret boards: Owner, Admin.

- Any Pin type can be saved: image Pin, video Pin, Idea Pin, product Pin, etc.
- Any public Pin can be saved given a pin ID.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "board_id": "string",
  "board_section_id": "string"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pin_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of a Pin.|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|body|body|[PinsSaveRequestCreate](#schemapinssaverequestcreate)|true|none|
|» board_id|body|string \| null|false|Unique identifier of the board to which the pin will be saved.|
|» board_section_id|body|string \| null|false|Unique identifier of the board section to which the pin will be saved.|

<h1 id="pinterest-rest-api-productgrouppromotions">product_group_promotions</h1>

View, create, update, or delete information about promoted product groups.

## Get product group promotions

<a id="opIdproduct_group_promotions/list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/product_group_promotions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/product_group_promotions`

List existing product group promotions associated with an ad account.

Include either ad_group_id or product_group_promotion_ids in your request.

**Note:** ad_group_ids and product_group_promotion_ids are mutually exclusive parameters.
Only provide one. If multiple options are provided, product_group_promotion_ids takes precedence over ad_group_ids. If none are provided, the endpoint returns an error.

<h3 id="get-product-group-promotions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bookmark|query|string|false|Cursor used to fetch the next page of items|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Maximum number of items to include in a single page.<br>See documentation on [Pagination](/docs/reference/pagination/) for more information.|
|order|query|[Pinterest.Lib.PaginationOrder](#schemapinterest.lib.paginationorder)|false|The order in which to sort the items returned: "ASCENDING" or "DESCENDING" by ID.<br>Note that higher-value IDs are associated with more-recently added items.|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|
|product_group_promotion_ids|query|[[Pinterest.Lib.IntegerFormatType](#schemapinterest.lib.integerformattype)]|false|List of Product group promotion Ids.|
|entity_statuses|query|[[EntityStatus](#schemaentitystatus)]|false|Entity status|
|ad_group_id|query|string|false|Ad group Id.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|ASCENDING|
|order|DESCENDING|
|entity_statuses|ACTIVE|
|entity_statuses|PAUSED|
|entity_statuses|ARCHIVED|
|entity_statuses|DRAFT|
|entity_statuses|DELETED_DRAFT|

## Get product group analytics

<a id="opIdproduct_groups/analytics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/product_groups/analytics?start_date=1970-01-01&end_date=1970-01-01&product_group_ids=string&columns=SPEND_IN_MICRO_DOLLAR&granularity=TOTAL' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/product_groups/analytics`

Get analytics for the specified product groups in the specified `ad_account_id`, filtered by the specified options.

- The token's user_account must either be the Owner of the specified ad account, or have one of the necessary roles granted to them via [Business Access](https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/share-and-manage-access-to-your-ad-accounts): Admin, Analyst, Campaign Manager.
- If granularity is not HOUR, you can pull data from up to 90 days before the current date in UTC time, with a maximum time range of 90 days.
- If granularity is HOUR, you can pull data from up to 8 days before the current date in UTC time, with a maximum time range of 3 days.

<h3 id="get-product-group-analytics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report start date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days back from today.|
|end_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report end date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days past start_date.|
|product_group_ids|query|[[ProductGroupIdType](#schemaproductgroupidtype)]|true|List of Product group Ids to use to filter the results.|
|columns|query|[[ReportingColumnSync](#schemareportingcolumnsync)]|true|Columns to retrieve, encoded as a comma-separated string. **NOTE**: Any metrics defined as MICRO_DOLLARS returns a value based on the advertiser profile's currency field. For USD, ($1/1,000,000, or $0.000001 - one one-ten-thousandth of a cent). it's microdollars. Otherwise, it's in microunits of the advertiser's currency.<br><br>For example, if the advertiser's currency is GBP (British pound sterling), all MICRO_DOLLARS fields will be in GBP microunits (1/1,000,000 British pound).<br><br>If a column has no value, it may not be returned.|
|granularity|query|[Granularity](#schemagranularity)|true|  TOTAL - metrics are aggregated over the specified date range.<br><br>  DAY - metrics are broken down daily.<br><br>  HOUR - metrics are broken down hourly.<br><br>  WEEK - metrics are broken down weekly.<br><br>  MONTH - metrics are broken down monthly|
|click_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a pin click action. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `30` days.|
|engagement_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for an engagement action. Engagements include saves, closeups, link clicks, and carousel card swipes. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `30` days. **Note:** This parameter no longer returns new data. However, you can still access historic data through **Sept 30, 2027**.|
|view_window_days|query|number|false|Number of days to use as the conversion attribution window for a view action. Applies to Pinterest Tag conversion metrics. Prior conversion tags use their defined attribution windows. If not specified, defaults to `1` day.|
|conversion_report_time|query|string|false|The date by which the conversion metrics returned from this endpoint will be reported. There are two dates associated with a conversion event: the date that the user interacted with the ad, and the date that the user completed a conversion event.|
|reporting_timezone|query|[ReportingTimeZone](#schemareportingtimezone)|false|Specify the timezone to be applied for the reporting. This feature is currently in BETA and is not available to all users.|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

## Add product tags to pin

<a id="opIdproduct_tags/bulk_add"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/pins/string/product_tags \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "product_tags": [
      {
        "pin_id": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /pins/{pin_id}/product_tags`

Add product tags to a pin. Product tags allow you to tag product pins onto a hero pin.
- Maximum 24 product tags can be added in a single request.
- Duplicate pin_ids in the request will result in an error.
- If any product tag fails eligibility check, the entire request fails (all-or-nothing).
- If a product tag is already tagged on the pin, it is treated as a no-op success.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "product_tags": [
    {
      "pin_id": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-product-tags-to-pin-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pin_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the hero pin that will receive product tags.|
|body|body|[ProductTagsBulkAddRequest](#schemaproducttagsbulkaddrequest)|true|none|
|» product_tags|body|[[ProductTagItem](#schemaproducttagitem)]|true|List of product tags to add. Maximum 24 items allowed.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "product_tags": [
    {
      "pin_id": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "details": {
    "product_tags": [
      {
        "error_message": {},
        "pin_id": "string"
      }
    ]
  },
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 2,
  "message": "AdAccount not found."
}
```

|400|Bad Request|The request contains ineligible product tags.|[ProductTagsError](#schemaproducttagserror)|

|default|Default|An unexpected error response.|[Pinterest.Lib.Error](#schemapinterest.lib.error)|

<h1 id="pinterest-rest-api-promotions">promotions</h1>

## Get promotions

<a id="opIdpromotions/list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/ad_accounts/string/promotions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/promotions`

Gets all promotions associated with an ad account ID that can be
applied to an ad group. Can be either internally-saved promotions or external
promotions imported from a commerce integration.

<h3 id="get-promotions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|bookmark|query|string|false|Cursor used to fetch the next page of items|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Maximum number of items to include in a single page.<br>See documentation on [Pagination](/docs/reference/pagination/) for more information.|
|order|query|[Pinterest.Lib.PaginationOrder](#schemapinterest.lib.paginationorder)|false|The order in which to sort the items returned: "ASCENDING" or "DESCENDING" by ID.<br>Note that higher-value IDs are associated with more-recently added items.|
|ad_account_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

`GET /resources/targeting/{targeting_type}`

    You can use targeting values in ads placement to define your intended audience.

`GET /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/targeting_templates`

<h3 id="list-targeting-templates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|include_sizing|query|boolean|false|Include audience sizing in result or not|

`POST /ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}/targeting_templates`

Targeting templates allow advertisers to save a set of targeting details including audience lists, keywords & interest, demographics, and placements to use more than once during the campaign creation process.

Templates can be used to build out basic targeting criteria that you plan to use across campaigns and to reuse performance targeting from prior campaigns for new campaigns.

      ],

        "string"
      ],
      "GEO_EXCLUDE": [
        "string"
      ],
      "INTEREST": [
        "string"
      ],
      "LOCALE": [
        "string"
      ],
      "LOCATION": [
        "string"
      ],
      "LOCATION_EXCLUDE": [
        "string"
      ],
      "MAXIMUM_AGE": "string",

## List related terms

<a id="opIdterms_related/list"></a>

## Returns editorial articles for a given region

<a id="opIdtrends_editorial_articles/list"></a>

`GET /trends/editorial_articles`

## Get product category details

<a id="opIdtrends_product_categories_details/list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/trends/product_categories/details?product_categories=ACCENT_TABLES&region=US' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /trends/product_categories/details`

  Enables advertisers to retrieve demographic information, related pins, and trend lines for specified product categories

<h3 id="get-product-category-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|product_categories|query|[[ProductCategoryEnum](#schemaproductcategoryenum)]|true|List of product categories|
|region|query|[ProductCategoryRegion](#schemaproductcategoryregion)|true|     The geographic region of interest. Only top product categories within the specified region will be returned.<br>     The `region` parameter is formatted as ISO 3166-2 country codes delimited by `+`.<br><br>    - `US` - United States<br>    - `GB+IE` - Great Britain & Ireland<br>    - `CA` - Canada|
|lookback_window|query|[ProductCategoryDetailLookbackWindow](#schemaproductcategorydetaillookbackwindow)|false|  Time period for historical data analysis in days. The lookback window defines how far back in time the API will analyze data to compute trend metrics.<br>  - `90` - Last 90 days (3 months)<br>  - `180` - Last 180 days (6 months)<br>  - `365` - Last 365 days (1 year)<br>  - `730` - Last 730 days (2 years)|
|engagement_type|query|[ProductCategoriesEngagementType](#schemaproductcategoriesengagementtype)|false|    Type of engagement metric to analyze.<br>- `ENGAGEMENT` - Overall engagement metric<br>- `OUTBOUND_CLICK` - Number of outbound clicks<br>- `SAVE` - Number of pin saves|

## Get a list of growing Shopping Product Categories

<a id="opIdtrends_product_categories_trending/list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/trends/product_categories/trending?region=US' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /trends/product_categories/trending`

  Get a list of growing Shopping Product Categories in ranked order allowing filtering by engagement type, vertical, age, and gender.

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-growing-shopping-product-categories-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|region|query|[ProductCategoryRegion](#schemaproductcategoryregion)|true|     The geographic region of interest. Only top product categories within the specified region will be returned.<br>     The `region` parameter is formatted as ISO 3166-2 country codes delimited by `+`.<br><br>    - `US` - United States<br>    - `GB+IE` - Great Britain & Ireland<br>    - `CA` - Canada|
|verticals|query|[[VerticalProductCategory](#schemaverticalproductcategory)]|false|List of verticals to filter by|
|ages|query|[[AgeTrendsBucket](#schemaagetrendsbucket)]|false|Age to filter by. If not provided, the results will be filtered by all ages.|
|genders|query|[[GenderBucket](#schemagenderbucket)]|false|Gender to filter by, If not provided, the results will be filtered by all genders.|
|engagement_type|query|[ProductCategoriesEngagementType](#schemaproductcategoriesengagementtype)|false|    Type of engagement metric to analyze.<br>- `ENGAGEMENT` - Overall engagement metric<br>- `OUTBOUND_CLICK` - Number of outbound clicks<br>- `SAVE` - Number of pin saves|

|Parameter|Value|

|region|US|
|region|GB+IE|
|region|CA|

|ages|65+|
|genders|MALE|
|genders|FEMALE|
|genders|UNSPECIFIED|
|engagement_type|ENGAGEMENT|
|engagement_type|OUTBOUND_CLICK|
|engagement_type|SAVE|

<h1 id="pinterest-rest-api-useraccount">user_account</h1>

## Get user account

<a id="opIduser_account/get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/user_account \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /user_account`

Get account information for the "operation user_account"
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

[Understanding Business Access]: https://developers.pinterest.com/docs/getting-started/using-business-access/ "Understanding Business Access"
If using Business Access: Specify an ad_account_id to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account". See [Understanding Business Access] for more information.

<h3 id="get-user-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

## Get user account analytics

<a id="opIduser_account/analytics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/user_account/analytics?start_date=1970-01-01&end_date=1970-01-01' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /user_account/analytics`

Get analytics for the "operation user_account"
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an ad_account_id to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account".

<h3 id="get-user-account-analytics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report start date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days back from today.|
|end_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report end date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days past start_date.|
|from_claimed_content|query|string|false|Filter on Pins that match your claimed domain.|
|pin_format|query|string|false|Pin formats to get data for, default is all.|
|app_types|query|string|false|Apps or devices to get data for, default is all.|
|content_type|query|string|false|Filter to paid or organic data. Default is all.|
|source|query|string|false|Filter to activity from Pins created and saved by your, or activity created and saved by others from your claimed accounts|
|metric_types|query|[[QuerymetrictypesItems](#schemaquerymetrictypesitems)]|false|Metric types to get data for, default is all.|
|split_field|query|string|false|How to split the data into groups. Not including this param means data won't be split.|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|from_claimed_content|OTHER|
|from_claimed_content|CLAIMED|
|from_claimed_content|BOTH|
|pin_format|ALL|
|pin_format|ORGANIC_IMAGE|
|pin_format|ORGANIC_PRODUCT|
|pin_format|ORGANIC_VIDEO|
|pin_format|ADS_STANDARD|
|pin_format|ADS_PRODUCT|
|pin_format|ADS_VIDEO|
|pin_format|ADS_IDEA|
|app_types|ALL|
|app_types|MOBILE|
|app_types|TABLET|
|app_types|WEB|

## Get user account top pins analytics

<a id="opIduser_account/analytics/top_pins"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pinterest.com/v5/user_account/analytics/top_pins?start_date=1970-01-01&end_date=1970-01-01&sort_by=ENGAGEMENT' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /user_account/analytics/top_pins`

Gets analytics data about a user's top pins (limited to the top 50).
- By default, the "operation user_account" is the token user_account.

Optional: Business Access: Specify an ad_account_id to use the owner of that ad_account as the "operation user_account".

<h3 id="get-user-account-top-pins-analytics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report start date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days back from today.|
|end_date|query|string(date)|true|Metric report end date (UTC). Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be more than 90 days past start_date.|
|sort_by|query|[TopPinsSortBy](#schematoppinssortby)|true|Specify sorting order for metrics|
|from_claimed_content|query|string|false|Filter on Pins that match your claimed domain.|
|pin_format|query|string|false|Pin formats to get data for, default is all.|
|app_types|query|string|false|Apps or devices to get data for, default is all.|
|content_type|query|string|false|Filter to paid or organic data. Default is all.|
|source|query|string|false|Filter to activity from Pins created and saved by your, or activity created and saved by others from your claimed accounts|
|metric_types|query|[[QuerymetrictypesItems](#schemaquerymetrictypesitems)]|false|Metric types to get data for, default is all.|
|num_of_pins|query|integer|false|Number of pins to include, default is 10. Max is 50.|
|created_in_last_n_days|query|number|false|Get metrics for pins created in the last "n" days.|
|ad_account_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier of an ad account.|

## Create a Brand Account

<a id="opIdbrand_accounts/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/business_access/business_hierarchy/string/brand_accounts \
  -X POST \

    "about": "string",

    "name": "string",

      "content_type": "image/jpeg",
      "data": "string"
    },
    "username": "string",
    "website": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /business_access/business_hierarchy/{business_hierarchy_id}/brand_accounts`

Create a Brand Account that will be a child business of a business hierarchy. Request must contain name, username, and country.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "about": "string",
  "country": "AD",
  "name": "string",
  "profile_image": {
    "content_type": "image/jpeg",
    "data": "string"
  },
  "username": "string",
  "website": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-brand-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

## List business employers for user

## Get business members

<a id="opIdget/business_members"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/businesses/string/members \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /businesses/{business_id}/members`

Get all members of the specified business. The return response will include the member's business_role and assets they have access to if assets_summary=TRUE

<h3 id="get-business-members-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|business_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the requesting business.|
|fetch_system_users|query|boolean|false|Fetches system users if True. Fetches regular user employees if False.|
|assets_summary|query|boolean|false|Include assets summary in the response if this is true.<br><br>The assets summary returns a dictionary representing a summary of the assets<br>for the business user ID, with information like the ad accounts and profiles<br>the user has permissions for and what those permissions are|
|business_roles|query|[[MemberBusinessRole](#schemamemberbusinessrole)]|false|A list of business roles to filter the members by. Only members whose roles are in the specified roles will be returned.|
|member_ids|query|string|false|A list of business members ids separated by comma.|
|start_index|query|integer|false|An index to start fetching the results from. Only the results starting from this index will be returned.|
|bookmark|query|string|false|Cursor used to fetch the next page of items|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Maximum number of items to include in a single page.<br>See documentation on [Pagination](/docs/reference/pagination/) for more information.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|business_roles|EMPLOYEE|
|business_roles|BIZ_ADMIN|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "bookmark": "string",
  "items": [
    {
      "assets_summary": {

## Get business partners

<a id="opIdget/business_partners"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/businesses/string/partners \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /businesses/{business_id}/partners`

Get all partners of the specified business.

If the assets_summary=TRUE and:
- partner_type=INTERNAL, the business assets returned are your business assets the partner has access to.
- partner_type=EXTERNAL, the business assets returned are your partner's business assets the partner has granted you
  access to.

<h3 id="get-business-partners-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|business_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the requesting business.|
|assets_summary|query|boolean|false|Include assets summary in the response if this is true.<br><br>The assets summary returns a dictionary representing a summary of the assets<br>for the business user ID, with information like the ad accounts and profiles<br>the user has permissions for and what those permissions are|
|partner_type|query|[PartnerType](#schemapartnertype)|false|Specifies whether to fetch internal or external (shared) partners.<br>If partner_type=INTERNAL, the asset being queried is for accesses the partner has to your business assets.<br>If partner_type=EXTERNAL, the asset being queried is for the accesses you have to the partner's business asset.|
|partner_ids|query|string|false|A list of business partner ids separated by commas used to filter the results. Only partners with the specified ids will be returned.|
|start_index|query|integer|false|An index to start fetching the results from. Only the results starting from this index will be returned.|
|sort_ascending|query|boolean|false|Sort ascending.|
|bookmark|query|string|false|Cursor used to fetch the next page of items|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Maximum number of items to include in a single page.<br>See documentation on [Pagination](/docs/reference/pagination/) for more information.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|partner_type|INTERNAL|
|partner_type|EXTERNAL|

## Create invites or requests

<a id="opIdcreate_membership_or_partnership_invites"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/businesses/string/invites \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "business_role": "BIZ_ADMIN",
    "invite_type": "MEMBER_INVITE",
    "members": [
      "business0101",
      "user@business.com"
    ],
    "partners": [
      "809944451643622187",
      "766456567741825556"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /businesses/{business_id}/invites`

Create batch invites or requests. Can create batch invites or requests as described below.
- Invite members to join the business. This would required specifying the following:
    - invite_type="MEMBER_INVITE"
    - business_role="EMPLOYEE" OR business_role="BIZ_ADMIN" (To learn more about business roles, visit
    https://help.pinterest.com/en/business/article/profile-permissions-in-business-access.)
    - members
- Invite partners to access your business assets. This would require specifying the following:
    - invite_type="PARTNER_INVITE"
    - business_role="PARTNER"
    - partners
- Request to be a partner so you can access their assets. This would require specifying the following:
    - invite_type="PARTNER_REQUEST"
    - business_role="PARTNER"
    - partners

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "business_role": "BIZ_ADMIN",
  "invite_type": "MEMBER_INVITE",
  "members": [
    "business0101",
    "user@business.com"
  ],
  "partners": [
    "809944451643622187",
    "766456567741825556"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-invites-or-requests-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|business_id|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the requesting business.|
|body|body|[CreateMembershipOrPartnershipInvitesBody](#schemacreatemembershiporpartnershipinvitesbody)|true|none|
|» business_role|body|object|true|none|
|» invite_type|body|[InviteType](#schemainvitetype)|true|The type of invite. MEMBER_INVITE invites a member to access your business assets. PARTNER_INVITE invites a partner to access your business assets. PARTNER_REQUEST requests access to a partner's business assets.|
|» members|body|[string]|false|A list of usernames, emails, or a mix of them. Should be used if invite_type is MEMBER_INVITE|
|» partners|body|[[BusinessInviteOrPartnerId](#schemabusinessinviteorpartnerid)]|false|A list of partner_id. Should be used if invite_type is PARTNER_INVITE or PARTNER_REQUEST|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» invite_type|MEMBER_INVITE|
|» invite_type|PARTNER_INVITE|
|» invite_type|PARTNER_REQUEST|

curl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/businesses/string/invites/assets/access \
