<h2 id="tocS_TrendingKeyword">TrendingKeyword</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematrendingkeyword"></a>
<a id="schema_TrendingKeyword"></a>
<a id="tocStrendingkeyword"></a>
<a id="tocstrendingkeyword"></a>

```json
{
  "demographics": {
    "age_distribution": {
      "age_distribution": "18-24",
      "property1": 0,
      "property2": 0
    },
    "gender_distribution": {
      "gender_distribution": "male",
      "property1": 0,
      "property2": 0
    }
  },
  "has_prediction": true,
  "keyword": "string",
  "pct_growth_mom": 0,
  "pct_growth_wow": 0,
  "pct_growth_yoy": 0,
  "predicted_time_series": {
    "date": "1970-01-01",
    "property1": 0,
    "property2": 0
  },
  "time_series": {
    "date": "1970-01-01",
    "property1": 0,
    "property2": 0
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|demographics|[TrendingKeywordDemographics](#schematrendingkeyworddemographics)|false|none|A mapping of demographic dimensions (e.g. "gender", "age") to their category<br>distributions. For each dimension: Key: The category (e.g., "female", "18-24").<br>Value: The proportion of search volume (e.g., 0.12 for 12%). Values less than<br>0.05 are set to 0.04 for privacy. The sum for all categories in a dimension<br>will approximately equal 1. Only applicable when `include_demographics` query<br>parameter is set to `true`.|
|has_prediction|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether the keyword has a prediction available for the next 90 days.<br>This field is only applicable when `include_prediction` query parameter is set<br>to `true`. By default, the value is `false` and no prediction data is included<br>in the response.|
|keyword|string|false|none|The keyword that is trending.|
|pct_growth_mom|integer|false|none|The month-over-month percent change in search volume for this keyword.<br>For example, a value of "400" would represent a 400% increase in searches<br>in the last 30 days compared to the month prior. **Note**: growth rates are<br>rounded, with a maximum of +/- 10000% change. A value of 10001 indicates<br>that this keyword experienced > 10000% month-over-month growth.|
|pct_growth_wow|integer|false|none|The week-over-week percent change in search volume for this keyword.<br>For example, a value of "50" would represent a 50% increase in searches<br>in the last seven days compared to the week prior. **Note**: growth rates<br>are rounded, with a maximum of +/- 10000% change. A value of 10001<br>indicates that this keyword experienced > 10000% week-over-week growth.|
|pct_growth_yoy|integer|false|none|The year-over-year percent change in search volume for this keyword.<br>For example, a value of "-5" would represent a 5% decrease in searches<br>in the last 365 days compared to the month prior. **Note**: growth rates<br>are rounded, with a maximum of +/- 10000% change. A value of 10001<br>indicates that this keyword experienced > 10000% year-over-year growth.|
|predicted_time_series|object|false|none|A sequence of weekly observations of the predicted relative search volume<br>for this keyword over the next 3 months. These values are normalized to a<br>[0-100] range, and can be used to visualize the forecasted user interest in<br>this keyword. Similar to the historical `time_series`, normalization is<br>applied independently to the predicted time series of each keyword, but the<br>`normalize_against_group` query parameter can be used in cases where you wish<br>to compare relative predicted volume between keywords.<br><br>**Note**: The cut-off date between historical and predicted time series<br>depends on Pinterest data availability. Usually the data needs a few days to<br>be calculated, so the predicted time series may contain some past dates<br>compared to today.<br><br>**Note**: The date of each observation is in ISO-8601 format and represents<br>the *end* of the week. For example, a value of `2024-01-07` would include<br>predicted searches for the week ending on `2024-01-07`.|
|time_series|object|false|none|A sequence of weekly observations of the relative search volume for this<br>keyword over the past year. These values are normalized to a [0-100] range,<br>and can be used to visualize the history of user interest in this keyword.<br>By default, normalization is applied independently to the time series of<br>each keyword, but the `normalize_against_group` query parameter can be used<br>in cases where you wish to compare relative volume between keywords.<br><br>**Note**: The date of each observation is in ISO-8601 format and represents<br>the *end* of the week. For example, a value of `2023-10-31` would include<br>searches that happened between `2023-10-25` and `2023-10-31`.|

<h2 id="tocS_TrendingKeywordDemographics">TrendingKeywordDemographics</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematrendingkeyworddemographics"></a>
<a id="schema_TrendingKeywordDemographics"></a>
<a id="tocStrendingkeyworddemographics"></a>
<a id="tocstrendingkeyworddemographics"></a>

```json
{
  "age_distribution": {
    "age_distribution": "18-24",
    "property1": 0,
    "property2": 0
  },
  "gender_distribution": {
    "gender_distribution": "male",
    "property1": 0,
    "property2": 0
  }
}
```

A mapping of demographic dimensions (e.g. "gender", "age") to their category
distributions. For each dimension: Key: The category (e.g., "female", "18-24").
Value: The proportion of search volume (e.g., 0.12 for 12%). Values less than
0.05 are set to 0.04 for privacy. The sum for all categories in a dimension
will approximately equal 1. Only applicable when `include_demographics` query
parameter is set to `true`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|age_distribution|[TrendsAgeDistribution](#schematrendsagedistribution)|false|none|This represents a mapping from age bucket to distribution of search volume<br>for a keyword. The sum of all values in this object should approximately be 1.|
|gender_distribution|[TrendsGenderDistribution](#schematrendsgenderdistribution)|false|none|This represents a mapping from gender to distribution of search volume<br>for a keyword. The sum of all values in this object should approximately be 1.|
